aiReview.tagline: Spec-driven specify, plan, and implement for AI agents
aiReview.description: Install as an Antigravity or Claude Code plugin to force spec-and-plan workflows before feature and bug-fix implementation.
pros: Public GitHub repo with Apache-2.0 license, README, CONTRIBUTING, and ~3.8k stars / 299 forks.
Documents install/uninstall for Antigravity (agy plugins) and Claude Code marketplace plugins.
Ships plugin.json, skills, and rules for a Context → Spec & Plan → Implement protocol.
cons: Depends on specific AI coding agents rather than being a general-purpose CLI.
awesome-list discovery only used the title with no surrounding description.

aiReview.summary: Small Gemini CLI extension that adds listen-mode commands so the CLI can act as a server. Niche, lightly documented, and low community traction; suitable only for Gemini CLI users who want that workflow.
evidence: Repo description: Turn Gemini-CLI into a server with /isten commands packaged as a Gemini-CLI extension.
README install: gemini extensions install https://github.com/automateyournetwork/GeminiCLI_Listen_Extension.git
Apache-2.0 license; 14 stars, 2 forks, 9 commits; listed from Piebald-AI awesome-gemini-cli READMEs.
uncertainty: Actual command surface, network bind behavior, and auth for listen mode are not documented in the README.
Maintenance cadence and compatibility with current Gemini CLI versions are unverified.
Whether /isten is a typo for /listen is unclear.
aiReview.tagline: Gemini CLI extension that turns the CLI into a server
aiReview.description: Install a Gemini CLI extension that adds listen-mode commands so the CLI can run as a server.
pros: GitHub-backed Gemini CLI extension with an Apache-2.0 license.
Installs via gemini extensions install from the repository URL.
Appears on curated awesome-gemini-cli extension lists.
cons: README is essentially install plus a one-line description with little usage or security detail.
Only 14 stars, 2 forks, 9 commits, and no releases.
Listen/server mode is underspecified relative to typical production CLI tooling.

aiReview.summary: Small Apache-2.0 Gemini CLI extension that exposes desktop capture (single-frame and streaming) via MCP and slash commands. README is minimal; stars and commit history are modest, and screen sharing to an LLM has inherent privacy risk.
evidence: Repo description: Share your screen with Gemini-CLI via MCP and custom slash commands.
README: gemini extensions install from GitHub; mentions single frame and streaming.
Listed as Screenshare on Piebald-AI/awesome-gemini-cli and awesome-gemini-cli-extensions.
Public Apache-2.0 repo with gemini-extension.json, commands/screenshare, and servers.
uncertainty: Cannot verify capture implementation quality, OS support, or MCP server behavior from README.
Maintenance cadence and last-commit date not fully confirmed beyond 14 commits on main.
Privacy handling of captured frames is undocumented.
aiReview.tagline: Desktop capture for Gemini CLI via MCP commands
aiReview.description: Install a Gemini CLI extension that captures single frames or streams the desktop through MCP and custom slash commands.
pros: GitHub-backed Gemini CLI extension listed in curated awesome-gemini-cli sources.
Apache-2.0 license with an install command via gemini extensions.
Described as supporting single-frame capture and streaming modes over MCP.
cons: README is a few lines with no usage, security, or dependency details.
Low activity: 21 stars, 4 forks, 14 commits, and no releases.
Screen capture to a model implies privacy exposure that is not documented.

aiReview.summary: GitHub Gemini CLI extension that wires Cisco pyATS via a testbed.yaml and a one-line install; niche, lightly starred, and docs are thin.
evidence: Repo description: An easy to install pyATS extension for Gemini CLI.
Install snippet: gemini extensions install https://github.com/automateyournetwork/pyATS_GeminiCLI_Extension.git
Apache-2.0 license; ~10 stars, 4 forks, 59 commits.
Discovered from Piebald-AI awesome-gemini-cli curated lists.
uncertainty: Exact MCP/server capabilities inside servers/ not fully reviewed.
Maintenance cadence and last-commit date not independently verified beyond GitHub page load.
How credentials in testbed.yaml are handled at runtime.
aiReview.tagline: Install pyATS into Gemini CLI with a testbed file
aiReview.description: Install a Gemini CLI extension that enables pyATS using PYATS_TESTBED_PATH and a customizable testbed.yaml.
pros: Public GitHub repo with Apache-2.0 license and install via gemini extensions install.
Documents PYATS_TESTBED_PATH and replacing testbed.yaml, including a DevNet CML sandbox default.
Listed in curated awesome-gemini-cli / extensions READMEs.
Has dozens of commits on main rather than a one-file gist.
cons: README is brief and does not document commands, MCP tools, or security of device credentials.
Low adoption signals (about 10 stars and 4 forks) and no GitHub releases.
Depends on Gemini CLI plus a local pyATS testbed; not a standalone CLI.

aiReview.summary: Small Apache-2.0 Gemini CLI extension that adds subnet calculation via gemini extensions install. Niche networking helper with few stars and a thin README.
evidence: GitHub About: An extension for GeminiCLI that performs subnet calculation.
Apache-2.0 license, 5 stars, 0 forks, 6 commits.
Install: gemini extensions install https://github.com/automateyournetwork/GeminiCLI_SubnetCalculator_Extension.git
Discovered from Piebald-AI awesome-gemini-cli curated READMEs.
uncertainty: Last commit recency and maintenance cadence not verified from activity page.
Accuracy of subnet math and MCP/server implementation not reviewed.
IPv6 support and command surface not documented.
aiReview.tagline: Gemini CLI extension for IPv4 subnet math
aiReview.description: Install a Gemini CLI extension that calculates subnets from the terminal using the official extensions command.
pros: Public GitHub repo with Apache-2.0 license.
Installs with gemini extensions install from the git URL.
Listed in curated awesome-gemini-cli extension lists.
cons: Only five stars, zero forks, and six commits.
README is a one-line description plus install command.
Depends on Gemini CLI rather than being a standalone CLI.

aiReview.summary: Gemini CLI extension that analyzes packet captures via RAG, MCP, and custom slash commands. Niche and listed in curated Gemini CLI extension lists, but the README is thin and install notes still say “in the future.”
evidence: GitHub About: Gemini CLI extension using RAG, MCP, and custom slash commands to analyze packet captures.
Apache-2.0 license; 20 stars, 1 fork, 66 commits on main.
Discovered from Piebald-AI awesome-gemini-cli and awesome-gemini-cli-extensions READMEs.
Install command: gemini extensions install https://github.com/automateyournetwork/GeminiCLI_Packet_Buddy_Extension.git
uncertainty: Actual MCP/RAG quality and packet-analysis accuracy were not verified.
Last-commit recency and ongoing maintenance beyond commit count were not confirmed.
Whether the extension install path is fully supported by current Gemini CLI is unclear.
aiReview.tagline: Gemini CLI extension for packet-capture analysis
aiReview.description: Adds RAG, MCP, and slash commands to Gemini CLI so you can inspect packet captures from the terminal.
pros: Public GitHub repo with Apache-2.0 license and 66 commits.
Stated purpose is packet-capture analysis using RAG, MCP, and custom slash commands.
Appears in curated Gemini CLI / extensions lists.
Includes gemini-extension.json plus commands and servers directories.
cons: README is mostly a one-line description and a placeholder install section labeled “in the future.”
Low community traction (about 20 stars and 1 fork).
Requires a Google API key; runtime behavior and maintenance are not documented in the README.

aiReview.summary: VS Code extension that launches Gemini, Claude, Codex, and Qwen CLIs in editor tabs and broadcasts one prompt to all of them. Small GitHub project with heavy marketing claims; it is an IDE wrapper, not a standalone CLI.
evidence: Repo d3j/gemini-cli-on-vscode: public, MIT, topics include vscode-extension and gemini-cli.
README documents MAGUS Council, editor-tab launch, command palette, and npm CLI prerequisites.
GitHub UI showed 16 stars, 7 forks, 33 commits at review time.
Discovered from Piebald-AI/awesome-gemini-cli README.
uncertainty: Marketplace install counts and extension quality were not verified.
Whether MAGUS Council works reliably across all four CLIs was not tested.
Maintenance cadence beyond 33 commits is unknown.
aiReview.tagline: Run multiple AI CLIs as VS Code editor tabs
aiReview.description: Launch Gemini, Claude, Codex, and Qwen CLIs in VS Code editor tabs and broadcast one prompt across them.
pros: Open-source MIT VS Code extension with TypeScript sources, tests, changelog, and bilingual README.
Integrates Gemini, Claude, Codex, and Qwen CLIs as editor tabs with batch launch and prompt broadcast.
Requires separately installed official CLIs rather than reimplementing model APIs.
Listed in Piebald-AI/awesome-gemini-cli.
cons: About 16 stars, 7 forks, and 33 commits; adoption is limited.
README uses unverified “world’s first” and “revolutionary” claims.
Depends on four global CLIs and vendor accounts; not a CLI itself.
Name and listing emphasize Gemini CLI while the product is a VS Code GUI wrapper.

aiReview.summary: Gemini CLI slash-command pack that starts a local HTTP listener (port 8765) so external POSTs, ngrok, and Slack can send events into the CLI, including MCP-aware replies. Small Apache-2.0 repo with copy-into-.gemini install, thin docs, and operational caveats around exposing the listener.
evidence: GitHub about: “A /listen feature for Gemini CLI”; Apache-2.0; 21 stars, 9 forks, 26 commits on main.
README installation: clone then copy commands and scripts into .gemini; usage lists /listen: start|status|stop|logs|health|help|clear|live.
README MCP, Slack slash, Slack Bolt, Whisper/attachments notes, and example curl POST to ngrok /event.
Discovered repeatedly from Piebald-AI/awesome-gemini-cli README.
uncertainty: Could not independently verify listener implementation quality, auth on port 8765, or maintenance cadence beyond commit/star counts.
Last-commit date and whether Gemini CLI still loads this command layout were not confirmed from facts.readme.
Slack Bolt path is described as “in the commands folder” while the tree also has slack_bolt at repo root.
aiReview.tagline: HTTP/Slack inbound events as Gemini CLI slash commands
aiReview.description: Add /listen to Gemini CLI: start a local event server, check status and logs, and forward Slack or HTTP messages into the CLI and MCP tools.
pros: Provides documented /listen subcommands for start, status, stop, logs, health, help, clear, and live mode on port 8765.
README describes HTTP POST testing via ngrok, MCP tool use on inbound messages, and Slack slash/Bolt integration.
Apache-2.0 licensed GitHub repo listed in Piebald-AI/awesome-gemini-cli with 26 commits.
Includes commands/listen, scripts, and a slack_bolt app plus env vars for Slack tokens and GEMINI_ENDPOINT.
cons: Install is a manual clone and copy of commands and scripts into ~/.gemini, not a packaged CLI.
Low adoption (21 stars, 9 forks) and README has typos plus a personal advocacy note rather than tests or versioned releases.
Usage depends on exposing a local listener (ngrok) and Slack bot tokens, which is easy to misconfigure.

aiReview.summary: A small GitHub collection of Gemini CLI custom slash-command TOML configs (productivity plus a few developer prompts). Useful as examples, but it is not a maintained CLI and has only one commit.
evidence: GitHub: amitkmaraj/gemini-cli-custom-slash-commands, ~167 stars, 15 forks, 1 commit on main.
README describes 10 commands (photo-rename, report-gen, email-draft, meeting-summary, file-organizer, task-prioritizer, test-gen, debug-assistant, security-audit, cleanup).
Install instructions copy .gemini/commands for Gemini CLI rather than publishing a binary or npm CLI.
Listed from Piebald-AI/awesome-gemini-cli curated README.
uncertainty: Actual TOML prompt quality and safety of shell commands inside configs not fully inspected.
License file not confirmed from the listing.
Ongoing maintenance after the initial commit is unknown.
aiReview.tagline: Gemini CLI slash-command configs for daily tasks
aiReview.description: Copy TOML slash commands into Gemini CLI for photos, reports, email, tests, debug, and cleanup workflows.
pros: Lists ten named slash commands with usage examples for general and developer tasks.
Documents copy-into-project or user-scoped ~/.gemini/commands install steps.
Public GitHub repo with a README and .gemini/commands layout.
Credits a Google Cloud blog post on Gemini CLI custom slash commands.
cons: Repository history shows a single commit, so maintenance is unverified.
It is configuration snippets, not a standalone command-line application.
Command behavior depends on Gemini CLI and local prompt quality, not shipped tests or releases.

aiReview.summary: Small Apache-2.0 Docker wrapper that runs Gemini CLI isolated with a bind-mounted project dir, optional preseed, and Context7 settings. Niche convenience image with very little adoption or commit history.
evidence: README describes docker run --rm -it -v ./:/app/ hlpr/gdcli and auto-init of ./llm/.gemini.store.
GitHub About: Gemini Dockerized CLI with small improvements; Apache-2.0; 4 stars.
Listed in Piebald-AI/awesome-gemini-cli curated README.
uncertainty: Image provenance and update cadence of hlpr/gdcli on Docker Hub were not verified.
Last-commit date and whether the image tracks upstream Gemini CLI were not confirmed beyond ~10 commits.
aiReview.tagline: Isolated Docker wrapper for Gemini CLI workflows
aiReview.description: Run Gemini CLI in a container with project mounts, auto-init of .gemini store, optional preseed, and Context7 API key support.
pros: Documents a one-line docker run and alias to invoke Gemini CLI with the current directory mounted.
Apache-2.0 licensed public GitHub repo with a Dockerfile and README usage notes.
Supports optional preseed mount and CONTEXT7_API_KEY for settings.
cons: Only 4 stars, 0 forks, and about 10 commits, so maintenance and community signal are weak.
Wrapper around another CLI rather than a standalone tool, with limited documented improvements.
No releases listed on GitHub from the public page.

aiReview.summary: Maintained Docker wrapper for Google Gemini CLI with Node and Bun images, UID mapping, and a documented shell-function workflow. Small GitHub following but active CI, versioned tags, and GPL-2.0 source.
evidence: Repo description and README: Gemini CLI as Docker so Node is not installed on the host.
Images: tgagor/gemini-cli with latest, alpine, version, and bun tags.
License GPL-2.0; CI workflow badge on main; topics include docker and gemini-cli.
uncertainty: Exact Docker Hub pull counts and image freshness beyond README badges.
Whether upstream Gemini CLI APIs stay compatible with each image rebuild.
aiReview.tagline: Run Gemini CLI in Docker without installing Node locally
aiReview.description: Wraps Gemini CLI in auto-updated Node or Bun Docker images with volume mounts, UID mapping, and a shell function for isolated use.
pros: README documents a shell function with workspace and ~/.gemini mounts, UID/GID mapping, and TTY/color handling.
Provides Node (amd64/arm64/armv7) and Bun (amd64/arm64) images with versioned and alpine tags on Docker Hub.
GitHub Actions build badge, 160 commits, Makefile/Dockerfiles, and GPL-2.0 license are present.
Listed in Piebald-AI/awesome-gemini-cli as Docker Gemini CLI.
cons: Only 19 stars and 4 forks, so community traction is limited.
It wraps Google Gemini CLI rather than implementing a standalone CLI.
macOS Docker Desktop mount/permission caveats are noted in the README.

aiReview.summary: MIT-licensed Rust CLI that lists, installs, and switches among AI coding-agent harnesses from one TUI/headless interface; GitHub-backed with npm/Cargo/Homebrew installs, modest stars, and explicit file/command-execution risk.
evidence: README describes a command center for coding-agent harnesses (Claude, Gemini, Qwen, etc.) with tui/list/show/use/run.
Install paths: cargo install, npm -g, Homebrew tap; MIT license; docs/, tests/, CI badges.
Repo topics include cli, agents, terminal; ~137 stars, 726 commits, listed in awesome-gemini-cli.
uncertainty: Current npm/crates download volume and release cadence not verified from the HTML overview.
Exact set of supported harnesses and maintenance of each adapter not fully enumerated from the truncated README.
No independent security audit of the wrapper or install scripts reviewed.
aiReview.tagline: Switch and run multiple AI coding CLIs from one terminal
aiReview.description: Install, inspect, and switch AI coding-agent harnesses via a TUI or headless CLI, with optional security gates.
pros: Rust CLI with TUI and headless commands for listing, installing, and switching coding-agent harnesses.
Distributed via Cargo, npm, and Homebrew with MIT license and substantial commit history.
Documents security gates (e.g. Trivy) and warns that wrapped tools can modify files and run commands.
cons: Community traction is modest (~137 stars, 18 forks).
Using it launches third-party agents that can change files and execute commands.
Requires installing and authenticating multiple external harnesses to be useful.

aiReview.summary: The listed URL is a personal puzzles-and-agent-skills repo; the Gemini CLI log HTML exporter is only a nested Python script, so the directory entry points at the wrong artifact.
evidence: GitHub description: Ideas, tricks, materials with puzzles for AIs; 17 stars, 2 forks, MIT.
Log tool lives at code/Gemini CLI logs prettifier/pretty_print_chat.py, not at repo root.
awesome-gemini-cli lists the repo as Gemini CLI Logs Prettifier despite mismatched primary README.
uncertainty: Script version, packaging, and Windows support were not executed locally.
Maintenance of the nested script versus the broader puzzle repo is unclear.
aiReview.tagline: Convert Gemini CLI JSON session logs to HTML
aiReview.description: Scans ~/.gemini/tmp JSON chat and checkpoint files and writes styled, interlinked HTML you can open in a browser.
pros: Includes a Python script that converts Gemini CLI JSON logs and checkpoints under ~/.gemini/tmp into styled HTML.
Nested README documents recursive scan, file:// links, and Ubuntu/Termux usage.
Repository is MIT-licensed and actively committed.
The log exporter was discussed in google-gemini/gemini-cli community threads.
cons: Canonical URL is the whole Puzzles_for_AIs project, not a dedicated CLI package.
The prettifier is a single script in a subdirectory, not an installable CLI.
Repo README focuses on AI puzzles and agent skills, not log prettification.
Windows path handling is noted as potentially needing local adaptation.

aiReview.summary: Archived experimental Python SDK that wraps Gemini CLI with a Claude Code SDK-compatible API. Low stars, early-dev caveats, and read-only status make it a weak directory listing unless you want historical/migration references.
evidence: GitHub about: Python SDK for Gemini CLI, API-compatible with Claude Code SDK.
Banner: archived by owner Sep 15, 2026; experimental warning in README.
Install via pip install gemini-cli-sdk; wraps npm @google/gemini-cli.
Stars 18, forks 3, MIT license, issues cited for JSON output and missing resume/hooks.
uncertainty: PyPI download/version health and last real release date.
Whether Gemini CLI JSON output migration ever completed.
Reason for archival and any successor project.
aiReview.tagline: Python wrapper for Gemini CLI, Claude SDK-compatible API
aiReview.description: Programmatically query Gemini CLI from Python with an async API designed to match Claude Code SDK imports and options.
pros: Public MIT-licensed Python package with README, tests, examples, and migration docs.
Documents an async query API and Claude Code SDK import/option aliases.
Lists prerequisites (Python 3.10+, Gemini CLI, API key) and known limitations.
cons: Repository was archived on Sep 15, 2026 and is read-only.
README marks the project experimental with API and parsing limitations.
Only 18 stars, 3 forks, and 19 commits, indicating limited adoption.

aiReview.summary: Archived TypeScript community provider that wired Vercel AI SDK to Gemini CLI OAuth; Google ended that path and the repo is deprecated, so it is a poor fit for an active directory.
evidence: GitHub banner: archived and read-only; README warning that the package is deprecated.
README maps remaining auth to @ai-sdk/google and @ai-sdk/google-vertex.
About: community Vercel AI SDK provider via Gemini Code Assist / CLI; 72 stars, 18 forks, MIT.
Source discovery from Piebald-AI/awesome-gemini-cli.
uncertainty: Exact npm download volume and last published version were not verified from npmjs.
Whether forks remain usable against Antigravity CLI was not checked.
aiReview.tagline: Vercel AI SDK provider using Gemini CLI OAuth
aiReview.description: Connects Vercel AI SDK to Gemini via Gemini CLI core and Cloud Code, with OAuth and API-key auth. Deprecated after CLI shutdown.
pros: MIT-licensed TypeScript package with README, examples, changelog, tests, and npm versioning for AI SDK v4–v6.
Documented createGeminiProvider usage for oauth-personal and API-key auth plus generateText.
Listed on a curated Gemini CLI awesome README.
cons: Repository was archived on Aug 3, 2026 and all npm versions are marked deprecated.
Core oauth-personal use case ended when Gemini CLI stopped serving individual-account requests on June 18, 2026.
It is an SDK library, not a maintained CLI utility.

aiReview.summary: FastAPI proxy that exposes Gemini CLI OAuth credentials as OpenAI-compatible and native Gemini HTTP APIs, including Docker and HF Spaces deploy. Useful for local prototyping, but it is a credential-forwarding quota workaround rather than an official SDK or CLI.
evidence: README title: Gemini CLI to API Proxy; FastAPI converting Gemini CLI into OpenAI-compatible and native Gemini APIs.
Features listed: streaming, multimodal, multiple auth methods, search/thinking model suffixes, Docker, HF Spaces.
Repo stats from GitHub: 590 stars, 626 forks, MIT, public, 57 commits.
Listed on Piebald-AI/awesome-gemini-cli curated README.
uncertainty: Last commit date and current build health.
Whether Google ToS allows this credential/quota reuse in practice.
Security of password-as-API-key and credential JSON handling in production.
aiReview.tagline: Gemini CLI OAuth as OpenAI-compatible HTTP APIs
aiReview.description: Run a FastAPI proxy that maps Gemini CLI credentials to OpenAI-style chat and native Gemini endpoints with streaming and Docker.
pros: README documents OpenAI-compatible /v1/chat/completions plus native Gemini generateContent and streaming endpoints.
Includes Docker, docker-compose, Hugging Face Spaces metadata, health check, and MIT license.
GitHub shows ~590 stars, ~626 forks, and 57 commits on main.
Auth and credential env vars (password plus OAuth JSON) are documented.
cons: GitHub About has no description or topics; the project is a proxy server, not a command-line app.
It routes Gemini CLI/OAuth credentials to reuse Google quota through unofficial API shapes, which may conflict with provider terms.
Maintenance recency and test coverage are not established from the listing page.

aiReview.summary: Termux installer and menu for a Gemini reverse proxy (fork of geminicli2api) with OpenAI-compatible endpoints. Weak default auth, a committed .env, and proxy/LAN-sharing design warrant caution before listing.
evidence: README: 为 Android Termux 用户提供一键部署 Gemini API 反向代理服务; based on gzzhongqi/geminicli2api.
Default key documented as 123; dual /v1/chat/completions and Gemini v1beta routes.
Repo shows LICENSE MIT, Setup.sh, run.py, src/, MapleMono.ttf, committed .env.
175 stars, 24 forks, 28 commits, no GitHub description.
uncertainty: Whether .env contains live secrets.
Maintenance cadence and security of the proxy versus upstream.
Whether the default password is changed in current releases.
aiReview.tagline: One-command Termux Gemini reverse-proxy with a menu UI
aiReview.description: Install and manage a Gemini API reverse proxy on Android Termux, exposing OpenAI-compatible and native Gemini endpoints.
pros: GitHub-backed MIT project with a Termux Setup.sh installer and interactive menu.
Documents OpenAI-compatible and native Gemini routes, streaming, and several auth methods.
Listed on awesome-gemini-cli; ~175 stars, 24 forks, 28 commits.
States it is a Termux-focused fork of geminicli2api.
cons: README advertises default API key 123 and LAN sharing of the proxy.
Repository includes a committed .env file.
GitHub About has no description or topics; README is marketing-heavy.
Functionality is a reverse proxy, not an official Gemini CLI.

aiReview.summary: Cloudflare Worker that wraps Gemini Code Assist/CLI OAuth into OpenAI-compatible HTTP endpoints. Useful as a proxy, not a terminal CLI; ToS and credential-reuse risk should be reviewed.
evidence: Repo description: Expose Gemini CLI endpoints as OpenAI API with Cloudflare Workers.
Listed in Piebald-AI/awesome-gemini-cli curated README.
README features OAuth2, OpenAI SDK compatibility, KV token cache, and gemini-2.5 models.
GitHub stats: ~895 stars, 205 forks, 143 commits on main.
uncertainty: License file not confirmed in this pass.
Last commit recency and production stability not independently verified.
Google ToS compliance of Code Assist proxying is not assessed.
aiReview.tagline: OpenAI-compatible Gemini proxy on Cloudflare Workers
aiReview.description: Deploy a Worker that maps Gemini CLI OAuth to OpenAI-style chat, vision, tools, and streaming.
pros: Public GitHub repo with README covering OAuth setup, models, Docker, and Wrangler deploy.
Documents OpenAI-compatible chat, vision, tool calling, streaming, and thinking controls.
Shows 895 stars, 205 forks, and 143 commits with src, examples, and wrangler.toml.
MIT-style open source layout with TypeScript, tests HTTP files, and docker-compose.
cons: It is an HTTP proxy Worker, not a command-line app despite gemini-cli naming.
Setup copies Gemini CLI oauth_creds.json and uses Code Assist free-tier access, which may conflict with Google terms.
Requires Cloudflare Workers plus a Google account already used with Gemini CLI.

aiReview.summary: MIT-licensed Python proxy that exposes Gemini CLI as a local OpenAI-compatible /v1/chat/completions service. Useful for CLI/API bridging, but it depends on a logged-in Gemini CLI and markets unpaid API access, which is a ToS and maintenance risk.
evidence: Repo description and README: wrap Gemini CLI as OpenAI-compatible API on port 8765.
Features: /v1/chat/completions, uvx zero-config, FastAPI + asyncio.
MIT license badge; Python 3.12+; tests/ directory present.
Discovered from Piebald-AI/awesome-gemini-cli curated README.
uncertainty: Cannot verify Google ToS compliance of CLI-to-API wrapping.
Cannot verify recency of last commit, CI status, or production reliability from the page snapshot.
Streaming, tool-calling, and full OpenAI API coverage are not fully enumerated in the excerpt.
aiReview.tagline: Local OpenAI-style API in front of Gemini CLI
aiReview.description: Run a FastAPI proxy that maps chat completions to Gemini CLI so OpenAI clients can call Gemini models locally.
pros: GitHub repo with MIT license, tests, pyproject.toml, and bilingual README.
Documents uvx/uv startup, port override, curl and OpenAI Python client examples.
Implements /v1/chat/completions and notes FastAPI plus asyncio concurrency.
Listed in Awesome Gemini CLI and has ~152 stars and 24 forks.
cons: Requires a separately installed, already-logged-in Gemini CLI rather than calling Gemini APIs directly.
README frames the project as using a free Gemini Pro model via API, which may conflict with Google terms.
Small commit history (about 20 commits) and dummy-key auth on a local HTTP port.
Network proxy setup is required in some regions and is a common failure point.

aiReview.summary: Archived Node.js CLI that exposes Gemini CLI tools as MCP and an OpenAI-compatible chat API; useful historically but no longer maintained after Jul 2026.
evidence: GitHub page states the repo was archived by the owner on Jul 2, 2026.
README describes MCP toolkit plus OpenAI-compatible /v1/chat/completions and /v1/models.
npm global install of @intelligentinternet/gemini-cli-mcp-openai-bridge and gemini-cli-bridge CLI.
About section: 138 stars, 29 forks, Apache-2.0, 17 commits, no description.
Discovered from Piebald-AI/awesome-gemini-cli curated README.
uncertainty: Whether the npm package still installs and works against current Gemini CLI.
Last real commit date vs archive date and ongoing security patches.
Accuracy of submodule pin google-gemini/gemini-cli@263884b.
aiReview.tagline: MCP and OpenAI API bridge for Gemini CLI tools
aiReview.description: Run a local server that exposes Gemini CLI tools over MCP and OpenAI-compatible chat completions with configurable security modes.
pros: GitHub-backed Node CLI with Apache-2.0 license, npm package, Dockerfile, and bilingual README.
Documents MCP tool exposure, OpenAI /v1/chat/completions compatibility, and four security modes including default read-only.
Listed on a curated gemini-cli awesome list and has 138 stars and 29 forks.
Warns that YOLO mode can execute tools without confirmation and recommends containers.
cons: Repository was archived on Jul 2, 2026 and is read-only with no GitHub description or topics.
Only 17 commits and a gemini-cli git submodule that can override a local install.
README clone URLs still point at gemini-cli-common-bridge, which may confuse users.
Bridge does not prompt for tool confirmation and is not sandboxed at runtime.

aiReview.summary: Maintained Rust local LLM proxy that unifies Claude, Codex, Gemini, and OpenAI-compatible backends for CLI tools; listed from awesome-gemini-cli and ships installers, CI, and docs, with incomplete upstream parity.
evidence: Repo description: Rust rewrite of CLIProxyAPI for Claude, Codex, Gemini and OpenAI-compatible providers.
README documents curl/irm installers, Homebrew/Scoop, dashboard on 127.0.0.1:8317, and mixed-provider config.
Discovered from Piebald-AI/awesome-gemini-cli curated README.
Topics include llm-proxy, gemini-cli, self-hosted, rust.
uncertainty: License SPDX identifier not confirmed from LICENSE file contents in this pass.
Production stability and security of management dashboard and credential storage not independently audited.
Current release cadence beyond the presence of a releases badge.
aiReview.tagline: Local LLM proxy for mixed CLI providers and APIs
aiReview.description: Run one local endpoint so CLI tools can mix Claude, Codex, Gemini, and OpenAI-compatible providers with API keys or accounts.
pros: GitHub-backed Rust rewrite of CLIProxyAPI with 816 commits, CI, Docker, Homebrew, Scoop, and install scripts.
Documents a local OpenAI/Anthropic/Gemini-compatible endpoint, dashboard, config.yaml, and client key vs management key split.
Includes CONTRIBUTING, SECURITY, LICENSE, and a published parity audit against the original project.
cons: Parity with CLIProxyAPI is incomplete (README: 835 covered, 707 partial, 145 missing of 1,687 items).
Star/fork counts are still small (38 stars, 3 forks) relative to commit volume.
Connecting subscription accounts may conflict with provider terms; not every model/tool combination is tested.

aiReview.summary: MIT-licensed Gemini CLI extension of slash-command prompt templates for common development tasks; listed in awesome-gemini-cli but README install paths still use placeholders and the repo has only three commits.
evidence: GitHub about: curated prompts installable as a Gemini CLI Extension.
README lists install via gemini extensions install/link and many /namespace:command examples.
Repo stats from page: 411 stars, 108 forks, 3 commits.
Discovered repeatedly from Piebald-AI/awesome-gemini-cli README.
uncertainty: Actual quality and safety of individual prompt files was not audited.
Whether published extension install name matches this GitHub path.
Recency of last commit beyond the three-commit history count.
aiReview.tagline: Slash-command prompt templates for Gemini CLI
aiReview.description: Install a Gemini CLI extension with categorized slash commands for review, docs, tests, debugging, architecture, and learning.
pros: Public GitHub repo with MIT license badge and Gemini CLI extension manifest.
Documents 30+ slash commands across review, docs, testing, debugging, architecture, learning, writing, and prompt engineering.
Appears in Piebald-AI/awesome-gemini-cli and has hundreds of stars and forks.
Can be installed as a Gemini CLI extension via gemini extensions install/link.
cons: Installation examples still use yourusername/prompt-library-extension placeholders instead of this repo.
History shows only three commits on main, so maintenance depth is thin.
It is a prompt-pack extension, not a standalone CLI utility.

aiReview.summary: MIT TypeScript MCP server that wraps Google’s Gemini CLI with three tools (search, chat, file analysis). Small but documented GitHub project with tests; depends on Gemini CLI and a yolo/skip-confirmation flag.
evidence: GitHub README: MCP wrapper exposing googleSearch, chat, analyzeFile.
Stars 101, forks 16, TypeScript, tests/ and changelog through 0.3.1.
Listed from Piebald-AI/awesome-gemini-cli curated README.
uncertainty: Cannot verify npm download volume, ongoing maintenance after 2025-07 changelog, or Gemini CLI auth/cost behavior.
Cannot audit security of subprocess invocation from source beyond README claims.
aiReview.tagline: MCP server wrapping Gemini CLI search, chat, files
aiReview.description: Expose Gemini CLI as MCP tools for Google search, chat, and multimodal file analysis via npx or Bun.
pros: README documents three tools, parameters, MCP client config, and Claude Code setup.
Repository includes integration tests, changelog, and an MIT license notice.
Installable via npx or local Bun; 101 stars and recent changelog entries (0.3.x).
Supports optional sandbox and model selection when invoking Gemini CLI.
cons: Requires Gemini CLI (or --allow-npx) and is a thin wrapper, not a standalone Gemini client.
Exposes a yolo option that skips confirmations, which can increase unintended CLI actions.
Small project with limited issue history; production robustness is not independently verified.

aiReview.summary: Small MIT Python MCP server that wraps a local Gemini CLI for Claude Code, exposing one run_gemini tool. Useful for agent workflows but modest stars, shell=True subprocess, and a 60s timeout.
evidence: GitHub InfolabAI/gemini-cli-mcp: Python, MIT, 30 stars, 2 forks, files include gemini_mcp_server.py and test_gemini_mcp.py.
README states it wraps local gemini CLI for Claude Code via FastMCP run_gemini.
Discovered repeatedly from Piebald-AI/awesome-gemini-cli.
uncertainty: Cannot verify recent commit cadence, test coverage, or whether prompts/paths are escaped.
Gemini CLI availability, quotas, and model flags (e.g. gemini-2.5-flash) may change.
aiReview.tagline: MCP wrapper that runs local Gemini CLI from Claude Code
aiReview.description: Expose Gemini CLI as an MCP tool so Claude Code can analyze files, dirs, or URLs via Gemini’s context window.
pros: MIT-licensed Python project with README, tests, uv lockfile, and Claude Code MCP config.
Single documented tool run_gemini takes prompt plus file, directory, or URL path.
Requires local Gemini CLI and uv; listed in awesome-gemini-cli.
cons: About 30 stars and one issue; activity and maintenance are hard to judge from listing alone.
README documents subprocess.run with shell=True, which raises command-injection risk if paths or prompts are unsanitized.
Gemini CLI timeout is 60 seconds, which may fail on large analyses.

aiReview.summary: Local-first MIT TypeScript memory layer with a CLI, MCP/hooks for Codex and Claude Code, HTTP/Python clients, and SQLite by default. Listed in awesome-gemini-cli only as a Gemini CLI setup guide, so the directory title does not match the full product.
evidence: README describes durable memory API, goodmemory CLI, local SQLite, MCP, and npm package goodmemory@0.8.3.
Repo has TypeScript, MIT license, CI/eval/release workflows, Python client, inspector-web app, and many docs including Gemini CLI setup.
Discovered from Piebald-AI/awesome-gemini-cli with anchor text Gemini CLI setup guide.
uncertainty: npm latest publish status and real-world install quality were not independently verified.
Security of host hooks and writeback paths was not audited beyond README claims.
aiReview.tagline: Local-first memory API and CLI for coding agents
aiReview.description: Store, recall, inject, audit, and delete agent memory locally via CLI, MCP, TypeScript, and Python without a hosted account.
pros: Provides a documented CLI (`setup`, `status`, inspector) plus remember/recall/forget APIs and Codex/Claude Code host wiring.
Default local SQLite storage with MIT license, CI workflows, ADRs, and bilingual README.
Includes TypeScript package exports, a Python client, Docker files, and explicit fail-closed benchmark-claim policy.
cons: GitHub popularity is modest (about 19 stars) relative to the size of the repo.
README states 0.8.3 has no allowlisted public benchmark claims.
Source listing text is a Gemini CLI setup guide, which understates the full project.

aiReview.summary: Rust CLI that gives AI coding agents a persistent, source-grounded wiki/memory layer (SQLite, MCP/skills, optional self-hosted team sync). Fits CLI tooling lists; modest stars and agent-centric setup warrant a light human pass.
evidence: Repo README: agent-driven proactive memory CLI; works with Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI, Copilot, etc.
License Apache-2.0; language Rust; CI badge; crates.io lwc and npm @i-xor/lwc.
Discovered from Piebald-AI/awesome-gemini-cli as LWC.
Team memory v0.19.5: local SQLite + self-hosted sync; LWC does not embed an LLM.
uncertainty: Ongoing maintenance cadence and production reliability of team sync.
Security of MCP/hook installers across all claimed agent hosts.
Whether npm/crates packages stay in lockstep with GitHub releases.
aiReview.tagline: Agent-operated wiki memory with citations, not RAG
aiReview.description: Give coding agents a SQLite-backed wiki to recall, cite, and update knowledge across sessions via CLI and MCP.
pros: Apache-2.0 Rust CLI with crates.io and npm packages, CI, and docs in multiple languages.
Designed as a machine interface for agents (MCP, skills, hooks) rather than a human note app.
Stores immutable sources, wiki pages, citations, and history in SQLite without requiring a vector database.
Includes team deploy docs, admin UI, benchmarks, and installers for several coding agents.
cons: GitHub popularity is modest (about 68 stars) relative to the size of the repo.
Routine use depends on agent skill/MCP install rather than a simple human-driven CLI workflow.
Team sync and full snapshots add operational cost that is not fully verifiable from the listing alone.

aiReview.summary: Small Neovim plugin that toggles Gemini CLI in a split and can send visual selections; thin wrapper with modest stars and a single extra issue.
evidence: GitHub: jonroosevelt/gemini-cli.nvim, Lua, 57 stars, 8 forks, 1 issue.
Listed in Piebald-AI/awesome-gemini-cli curated README.
README states Neovim >= 0.7.0 and Node.js/npm requirements.
uncertainty: License file and last-commit recency were not inspected beyond the README snapshot.
Security of the install-prompt path was not reviewed in source.
aiReview.tagline: Toggle Gemini CLI in a Neovim split
aiReview.description: Open Gemini CLI in a Neovim split, send visual selections, and set EDITOR to nvim for in-session edits.
pros: README documents lazy.nvim, packer, and vim-plug setup plus split_direction config.
Features include CLI presence check, optional install prompt, and EDITOR=nvim for Gemini sessions.
Keymaps for toggle (<leader>og) and sending visual selection (<leader>sg) are documented.
cons: Repository is small (Lua plugin plus vim shim) with 57 stars and limited community signal.
Depends on an external gemini CLI and Node.js rather than implementing the CLI itself.

aiReview.summary: Proof-of-concept Gemini CLI config that orchestrates prompt-defined sub-agents via filesystem state and custom /agents commands. Useful as an example, not a maintained production CLI.
evidence: README title: Gemini CLI Prompt-Driven Sub-Agent Orchestrator; 91 stars, 26 forks.
Commands: /agents:start, run, status, type; state in .gemini/agents.
Disclaimer: not secure for production; relies on -y/--yolo.
uncertainty: License file not confirmed from the listing.
Maintenance cadence and issue quality beyond 3 open issues.
Whether the demo still works against current Gemini CLI.
aiReview.tagline: Prompt-driven Gemini CLI sub-agent orchestration demo
aiReview.description: Shows filesystem-as-state agent tasks using Gemini CLI custom commands, extensions, and background PIDs. Explicitly experimental and not production-safe.
pros: Documents architecture, commands, and an example workflow with screenshots.
Includes .toml custom commands, agent extensions, and a PRD.
Open GitHub repo with README, media, and a linked blog/demo.
cons: Author states it is a proof-of-concept and not secure for production because it uses --yolo.
Depends on Gemini CLI custom commands rather than shipping a standalone CLI.
Official Gemini CLI agentic features are noted as on the roadmap, so this may age quickly.
