aiReview.summary: GitHub markdown guide of ~30 tips for Google’s Gemini CLI (GEMINI.md, slash commands, MCP, YOLO mode). High-signal learning resource, not a CLI itself.
evidence: Repo about: Gemini CLI Tips and Tricks; README titled Gemini CLI Tips & Tricks.
README documents npm install -g @google/gemini-cli and interactive gemini usage.
Discovered from Piebald-AI/awesome-gemini-cli curated README.
uncertainty: License file not confirmed from the listing.
Last-commit date and ongoing accuracy vs current Gemini CLI not verified in full.
aiReview.tagline: Pro tips for Google’s terminal coding agent
aiReview.description: Open guide covering setup, persistent context, custom commands, MCP, scripting, and safety for Google’s agentic terminal assistant.
pros: Maintained public GitHub repo by Addy Osmani with ~2.4k stars, 105 forks, and 28 commits.
Structured README with a table of contents covering about 30 practical tips.
Lists real CLI patterns such as GEMINI.md, custom slash commands, MCP, checkpointing, and headless mode.
cons: It is a tips document, not a command-line app or SDK.
Some content cites third-party cheatsheets and may drift as Gemini CLI changes.
Tips include YOLO auto-approve and shell execution that need careful use.

aiReview.summary: Personal GitHub collection of Gemini CLI custom commands, extensions, and settings with clone-and-rsync install; small history (6 commits) and mostly documentation plus one command path.
evidence: GitHub description: Collection of helpful gemini cli extensions and commands.
README title: My Gemini CLI Extensions, Commands, and Settings; clone+rsync install commands.
Repo stats from page: 147 stars, 7 forks, 6 commits, Apache-2.0.
uncertainty: Cannot verify last-commit date or whether the plan command is actively maintained.
Cannot verify runtime quality of bundled commands without executing Gemini CLI.
aiReview.tagline: Personal Gemini CLI commands, extensions, and settings
aiReview.description: Install a personal set of Gemini CLI custom commands, extensions, and settings globally or per project via git clone and rsync.
pros: Apache-2.0 licensed public repo with README covering global and project install.
Documents custom TOML commands, gemini-extension.json, settings.json, and GEMINI.md usage.
Listed on a curated awesome-gemini-cli README and has 147 stars.
cons: Only six commits and a thin tree besides README, LICENSE, and .gemini/commands/plan.
Install uses rsync that may overwrite existing Gemini config files with the same names.
Content is a personal config dump rather than a maintained standalone CLI product.

aiReview.summary: GitHub example that wires Gemini CLI to Vertex AI Genmedia MCP servers (Imagen 4, Veo 3, image edit) for iterative video generation. Experimental, low-activity demo with heavy GCP setup; listed as an example, not a standalone CLI.
evidence: Repo description and README: example of Gemini CLI with MCP Servers for Genmedia and Gemini 2.5 Flash Image.
GitHub stats from page: 19 stars, 6 forks, 4 commits, Apache-2.0.
README NOTE: demonstration not intended for production; all assets and code AI-generated.
Discovered from Piebald-AI/awesome-gemini-cli curated README.
uncertainty: Cannot verify last-commit date, issue activity, or whether MCP config still matches upstream Creative Studio.
Cannot verify Vertex AI/Imagen/Veo API costs or current model availability.
aiReview.tagline: Gemini CLI example for Imagen/Veo video workflows
aiReview.description: Shows Gemini CLI plus Genmedia MCP servers for iterative image and video generation on Vertex AI, with sample prompts and assets.
pros: Apache-2.0 public repo with README setup for Gemini CLI, gcloud, Vertex AI, GCS, and MCP Genmedia servers.
Includes sample .gemini settings, prompts, generated image/video folders, and staged video-generation notes.
Uses Imagen 4, Veo 3, and gemini-2.5-flash-image-preview for consistency, as stated in the README.
cons: README labels it an experimental vibe-coding demo, not for production; demo video is still TODO.
Only 4 commits, 19 stars, and 6 forks; requires cloning a second Google repo and non-trivial GCP IAM.
States all media and code in the repository are AI-generated.

aiReview.summary: GitHub collection of boxed Gemini CLI demos (slides, SQLite, Sheets, git, ADK) for learning, not a standalone CLI; explicitly demo-only and not for production.
evidence: GitHub about: Demos-in-a-box for Gemini CLI.
README lists demos such as sqlite-investigation, auto-slide-creator, and adk-with-skills.
14 stars, 40 forks, 318 commits on palladius/gemini-cli-demos.
Discovered from Piebald-AI/awesome-gemini-cli curated README.
uncertainty: License SPDX identifier not confirmed from LICENSE file contents.
Currency of each demo against latest Gemini CLI releases not verified.
Whether npx package name in README is accurate was not independently checked.
aiReview.tagline: Boxed Gemini CLI examples for workshops and learning
aiReview.description: Collects repeatable Gemini CLI demos with GEMINI.md, scripts, and READMEs for agents, git, SQLite, and Google Workspace.
pros: Repository documents multiple categorized demos with status flags and per-demo folders.
Contribution guidance requires GEMINI.md, SCRIPT.md, README, purpose, and tests.
Has 318 commits, LICENSE, CHANGELOG, and a justfile-driven README update flow.
README states the project is for demonstration only, not production.
cons: It is example material, not a maintained command-line product.
Only 14 stars; several demos are marked incomplete or in-progress.
Install instructions point at npx @gemini/gemini-cli rather than shipping this repo as a tool.

aiReview.summary: GitHub cookbook of Gemini CLI demo scenarios with per-demo READMEs, starter materials, and asciinema recordings. It is example content rather than a maintained CLI utility.
evidence: GitHub About: Collection of demo scenario and casts for Gemini CLI.
README describes cookbook demos with README, starting materials, and asciinema .cast files.
Folders include java-runtime-modernize, python-http-client-modernize, tools, usage-sessions.
Listed from Piebald-AI/awesome-gemini-cli curated README.
uncertainty: Last commit recency and demo accuracy versus current Gemini CLI were not verified beyond the public page.
Quality of individual demo recordings and starter code was not executed.
aiReview.tagline: Repeatable Gemini CLI demo scenarios and recordings
aiReview.description: Clone demo folders with docs, starter code, and asciinema casts that show Gemini CLI on software engineering tasks.
pros: Apache-2.0 licensed public repository with README, contributing, CoC, and security files.
Each demo is a subfolder with documentation, starter materials, and a .cast recording.
Points to official Gemini CLI install docs rather than shipping a competing tool.
cons: Not a command-line app; it is demo/example material for another CLI.
Very small community signal (about 11 stars, 4 forks, 13 commits).
No releases; usefulness depends on keeping demos in sync with Gemini CLI.

aiReview.summary: GitHub markdown guide of personal Antigravity CLI tips (aliases, statusline script, AGENTS.md, voice, MCP). Useful as a companion resource, not a CLI product; small star count and opinionated workflow notes.
evidence: Repo description: Tips for using Antigravity CLI.
README covers aliases, statusLine command in ~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/settings.json, AGENTS.md, voice tools, Playwright MCP.
107 commits, content/ and scripts/ directories, 11 stars.
uncertainty: License file not confirmed from the listing.
Whether Antigravity CLI APIs in the tips remain current.
Maintenance cadence beyond commit count.
aiReview.tagline: Personal tips and scripts for Antigravity CLI
aiReview.description: Documents aliases, a custom status line, AGENTS.md, voice input, and agent verification workflows for Google’s Antigravity CLI.
pros: Public GitHub repo with a structured README of numbered CLI tips and example configs.
Includes a copyable status-line shell script under scripts/ plus AGENTS.md examples.
Linked from awesome-gemini-cli as Antigravity CLI Tips.
cons: It is a tips collection, not a maintained command-line application.
Low social proof (about 11 stars, 2 forks) and content is personal workflow advice.
Depends on Antigravity CLI paths and features that readers must already have installed.

aiReview.summary: Maintained GitHub awesome-list of Gemini CLI tools, forks, UIs, MCP servers, and related agent CLIs. Useful as a discovery resource, not as a command-line product itself.
evidence: GitHub description: curated list of tools, extensions, and resources for Gemini CLI.
About: 522 stars, 205 forks, 334 commits, CC0-1.0, topics include awesome-list and gemini-cli.
README contents cover Official, Interfaces, Forks, Agent Orchestration, MCP Servers, and more.
uncertainty: Recency of last commit and broken-link rate were not fully audited.
Whether listed commercial products remain accurate or affiliate-driven is unclear.
aiReview.tagline: Curated catalog of Gemini CLI tools and extensions
aiReview.description: Browse official Gemini CLI links plus community UIs, forks, orchestration tools, MCP servers, and docs in one GitHub list.
pros: Public GitHub repo with 500+ stars, 200+ forks, and hundreds of commits.
README is sectioned (official, interfaces, forks, orchestration, MCP, docs) with many linked projects.
Licensed CC0-1.0 with CONTRIBUTING.md.
Points at the official google-gemini/gemini-cli repository.
cons: It is a curated list, not a CLI or terminal utility.
The README leads with vendor promotion for Piebald and includes several UTM-tagged commercial links.
Link quality and maintenance of listed third-party projects are not independently verified here.

aiReview.summary: Gemini CLI extension that generates, edits, and restores images via Nano Banana / Gemini image models, with slash commands and an MCP server. Requires Node 20+, Gemini CLI, and a Gemini API key.
evidence: README: Nano Banana Gemini CLI extension for text-to-image, editing, restoration, and extra slash commands.
License Apache-2.0; Node 20+; gemini extensions install from this GitHub URL.
Public repo ~1.1k stars, 130 forks, 23 commits; mcp-server and gemini-extension.json present.
uncertainty: Release cadence and issue health beyond 23 commits not fully verified.
Actual model availability and API costs depend on Google’s Gemini offering.
aiReview.tagline: Image generate, edit, restore in Gemini CLI
aiReview.description: Install a Gemini CLI extension to generate, edit, restore, and batch images with Nano Banana models and slash commands.
pros: Apache-2.0 GitHub repo with README, changelog, security policy, and contributing docs.
Documents install via gemini extensions install plus commands such as /generate, /edit, and /restore.
Includes an MCP server (index.ts) and TypeScript modules for API and file handling.
About 1.1k stars and 130 forks; 23 commits on main.
cons: Needs a paid or quota-limited Gemini API key via NANOBANANA_API_KEY.
GitHub listing has no repository description or topics.
Tied to Gemini CLI and specific preview image model IDs.

aiReview.summary: Tiny MIT Gemini CLI extension that points an MCP client at Blender on localhost:9876 with trust enabled; README is one sentence and the repo has almost no code or docs.
evidence: Repo description and README: super simple extension to enable Blender via MCP for Gemini CLI.
gemini-extension.json name blender-mcp, version 0.1.0, mcpServers.blender.httpUrl http://localhost:9876, trust true.
GitHub metadata: 10 stars, 4 forks, 5 commits, MIT license, no releases.
uncertainty: Cannot verify whether the local Blender MCP server is documented or maintained elsewhere.
Last-commit recency and real-world usage beyond listing in awesome-gemini-cli-extensions are not confirmed.
aiReview.tagline: Wire Gemini CLI to a local Blender MCP server
aiReview.description: Gemini CLI extension JSON that registers a Blender MCP server at http://localhost:9876 with trust enabled.
pros: Public GitHub repo with an MIT license.
Manifest is a small gemini-extension.json that registers a Blender MCP HTTP endpoint.
Listed in a curated Gemini CLI extensions README.
cons: README is a single-sentence description with no install, usage, or Blender MCP setup steps.
Only five commits, ten stars, and no releases or tests.
Sets "trust": true for a localhost MCP server, which is a notable security default.

aiReview.summary: GitHub Gemini CLI extension that wires webcam/iPhone capture, ASL burst frames, and image/video generation into slash commands and natural-language prompts. Modest stars and a specialized Gemini-CLI-only audience make it a reasonable list entry after a maintainer check.
evidence: Repo description: Extension for Gemini-CLI with webcam access, single-frame capture, and ASL modes.
README documents gemini extensions install, /vision:devices|start|status|capture|burst|stop, banana, and veo.
License shown as Apache-2.0; public repo automateyournetwork/GeminiCLI_Vision_Extension.
Discovered from curated awesome-gemini-cli-extensions README.
uncertainty: Last-commit recency and issue health beyond HTML snapshot.
Runtime quality of ASL recognition and Veo/Banana API costs.
Windows/Linux camera support beyond macOS-focused docs.
aiReview.tagline: Webcam, ASL, and AI image/video from Gemini CLI
aiReview.description: Connect a webcam or tethered camera to Gemini CLI for capture, ASL bursts, and image or video generation via slash commands.
pros: Apache-2.0 GitHub repo with documented /vision:* commands for devices, start/stop, capture, burst, Banana image, and Veo video.
Install path is gemini extensions install from the repository URL.
README covers macOS camera permissions, natural-language usage, and static-image fallbacks.
Listed as Vision on Piebald-AI/awesome-gemini-cli-extensions.
cons: Community traction is modest (about 51 stars, 6 forks, 38 commits).
Depends on Gemini CLI, local camera access, and Gemini image/video APIs rather than a standalone CLI.
ASL and camera backends are environment-specific and not independently verified here.

aiReview.summary: Small Gemini CLI extension for voice input and OpenAI-backed TTS output; README is a one-command install with little usage or maintenance detail.
evidence: GitHub description and README: voice input and audio output; OpenAI required for TTS.
Install snippet: gemini extensions install https://github.com/automateyournetwork/GeminiCLI_Talk_Extension.git
Repo stats from GitHub: 5 stars, 3 forks, Apache-2.0, 8 commits, gemini-extension.json present.
Discovered from Piebald-AI/awesome-gemini-cli-extensions as Talk.
uncertainty: Cannot verify code quality, STT stack, or OpenAI usage without reviewing servers/commands.
Last-commit recency and ongoing maintenance not confirmed beyond 8 commits.
Runtime security of MCP/server components not audited.
aiReview.tagline: Voice in and TTS out for Gemini CLI
aiReview.description: Adds voice input and OpenAI TTS audio output to Gemini CLI via a git-installable extension.
pros: Apache-2.0 GitHub repo listed in awesome-gemini-cli-extensions.
Installs with gemini extensions install from the repository URL.
Stated purpose is voice input plus audio output for Gemini CLI, with OpenAI required for TTS.
cons: README is two short sections and does not document commands, env vars, or failure modes.
Only 5 stars, 3 forks, and 8 commits; no releases.
TTS depends on a third-party OpenAI key, which is not configured in the docs.

aiReview.summary: GitHub Gemini CLI extension that exposes Computer Use via MCP so the CLI can drive a browser (headful/headless) with screenshots and scripted prompts. Fits a Gemini CLI extensions list, but computer-use automation carries elevated operational risk.
evidence: Listed under Computer use in Piebald-AI/awesome-gemini-cli-extensions.
Repo about: A Google Gemini-CLI extension than enables Gemini Computer Use from the CLI.
Structure includes commands/ComputerUse, servers, GEMINI.md, LICENSE Apache-2.0.
uncertainty: Maintenance cadence and Gemini CLI API compatibility over time.
Whether MCP server code sanitizes actions or limits domains.
Exact runtime dependencies (browser binaries, API keys) beyond README excerpts.
aiReview.tagline: Gemini CLI extension for MCP-driven browser computer use
aiReview.description: Installs as a Gemini CLI extension so the model can initialize a browser, scroll, click, and capture state for visible or headless browsing.
pros: Public GitHub repo with Apache-2.0 license, README, gemini-extension.json, and example ComputerUse commands.
Install path is documented as gemini extensions install from the GitHub URL.
README includes concrete MCP-style prompts for headful browsing, scrolling, snapshots, and Markdown reports.
cons: Modest traction (~91 stars, 32 commits) and a typo in the official description.
Computer-use / headful browser control can execute arbitrary page actions if the model is unconstrained.
Examples are long prompt scripts rather than a polished productized CLI UX.

aiReview.summary: Official Gemini CLI extension repo under the Figma org, but it is archived (Mar 2026) and explicitly deprecated in favor of an MCP server guide. Poor fit for a maintained CLI/tools list until the listing points at the successor.
evidence: GitHub page: Public archive, archived Mar 26, 2026; About links to figma/mcp-server-guide.
README title: DEPRECATED Gemini CLI Extension; instructs bookmark and workflow migration to MCP.
License: Apache-2.0; 124 stars, 10 forks, 8 commits.
Discovered from Piebald-AI/awesome-gemini-cli-extensions as anchor text Figma.
uncertainty: Whether the awesome list has already been updated to the MCP successor.
Runtime quality of the old gemini-extension JSON versus current Gemini CLI APIs.
Exact last commit date beyond archive announcement.
aiReview.tagline: Archived Gemini CLI extension; use MCP successor
aiReview.description: Deprecated Gemini CLI extension for design-tool workflows. Repo is archived; functionality moved to an MCP-based setup.
pros: Hosted under the official figma GitHub organization with an Apache-2.0 license.
README states the extension was migrated to a Model Context Protocol implementation and links the successor repo.
Listed on a curated awesome-gemini-cli-extensions source.
cons: Repository is a public archive (read-only as of 2026-03-26) with no further updates or security patches.
README marks the project deprecated and tells users to switch to github.com/figma/mcp-server-guide.
Only eight commits, 124 stars, and 10 forks, with almost no remaining code besides README and an old extension JSON.

aiReview.summary: Archived Gemini CLI extension that searches Google Fonts and Material Icons via local tools. Listed in awesome-gemini-cli-extensions but the repo is read-only as of Oct 2025, so it is a weak fit for a maintained CLI directory.
evidence: GitHub About: Gemini CLI extension for Google Fonts + Material Icons and Symbols.
Banner: This repository was archived by the owner on Oct 27, 2025.
README lists search_fonts, search_icons, search_font_tags, get_icon_categories, get_icon_styles.
Apache-2.0 license; 24 commits; listed from Piebald-AI/awesome-gemini-cli-extensions.
uncertainty: Whether Gemini CLI still loads archived extensions.
Freshness of google_fonts.sqlite versus current Google Fonts catalog.
Runtime quality of the MCP/tools implementation beyond README claims.
aiReview.tagline: Search Google Fonts and Material Icons in Gemini CLI
aiReview.description: Install as a Gemini CLI extension to search fonts, tags, and Material Icons from a local database without leaving the terminal.
pros: Apache-2.0 GitHub repo with documented search_fonts, search_icons, and related tools.
Includes tests, TypeScript config, and a local google_fonts.sqlite catalog.
Install path is a single gemini extension install command.
cons: Repository was archived on Oct 27, 2025 and is now read-only.
Very small community signal (about 13 stars, 0 forks).
Requires Node.js v24+ and only works inside Gemini CLI, not as a standalone CLI.

aiReview.summary: Official-looking Gemini CLI extension that proxies GitLab SaaS MCP for issues, MRs, pipelines, and search. Small, young repo (few commits/stars) with tests and Apache-2.0 docs; worth a human look before listing.
evidence: GitHub about: GitLab extensions for Gemini CLI; topics ai, gemini, gitlab.
README: connects to https://gitlab.com/api/v4/mcp without a local Ruby runtime.
Repo has commands/, src/, tests/, package.json, Apache 2.0.
uncertainty: Whether GitLab-Ecosystem is an official GitLab org and how actively the repo is maintained.
Whether mcp_server / oauth_dynamic_client_generation flags are generally available.
License file presence vs README-only Apache 2.0 claim not fully verified as a blob.
aiReview.tagline: Gemini CLI commands for issues, MRs, and pipelines
aiReview.description: Installable Gemini CLI extension that maps slash commands to a hosted MCP for issues, merge requests, pipelines, and search.
pros: README documents install via gemini extensions, Node 20+, and Gemini CLI v0.8.0+.
Defines slash commands for issues, merge requests, pipelines, notes, and search.
Includes tests, TypeScript build, Apache 2.0 license, and gemini-extension.json at the repo root.
cons: Only 15 stars, 3 forks, and 5 commits on the default branch.
Requires SaaS feature flags, OAuth browser login, and npx mcp-remote on first run.
Distribution notes still mention an alternate install path that may confuse users.

aiReview.summary: Official Google Gemini CLI extension that adds /code-review and /pr-code-review commands for analyzing local branch or GitHub PR diffs. Apache-2.0, listed in awesome-gemini-cli-extensions; depends on Gemini CLI ≥0.4.0 and GitHub MCP for PR reviews.
evidence: GitHub about: Google's Code Review extension for the Gemini CLI that reviews your code changes.
README documents gemini extensions install, /code-review, /pr-code-review, Apache 2.0, ~532 stars and 41 forks.
Discovered repeatedly from Piebald-AI/awesome-gemini-cli-extensions README.
uncertainty: Exact review quality, issue types, and false-positive rates.
Ongoing maintenance cadence beyond the small commit count.
Whether Gemini API/CLI usage incurs paid quotas.
aiReview.tagline: Gemini CLI commands that review branch and PR diffs
aiReview.description: Install a Gemini CLI extension that reviews local branch changes and GitHub pull requests for code quality issues.
pros: Public GitHub repo under gemini-cli-extensions with Apache-2.0 license and documented install via gemini extensions install.
Adds /code-review for current-branch diffs and /pr-code-review for GitHub PRs with env vars or PR URL.
Tied to the same authors as the Gemini Code Assist GitHub App; README covers Gemini CLI version requirement and GitHub MCP setup.
cons: Requires Gemini CLI v0.4.0+ and Gemini usage; PR review also needs the GitHub MCP server and repository context.
Repository history is short (about 12 commits) and there are no GitHub Releases listed.
Effectiveness of reviews depends on the model and is not independently evaluated here.

aiReview.summary: Google-maintained Gemini CLI extension that adds /security:analyze and OSV-based /security:scan-deps for reviewing diffs and pull requests. Fits a curated CLI/extensions list; treat output as a first-pass scan, not a full audit.
evidence: GitHub about: Google's Security extension for Gemini CLI that finds vulnerabilities in code changes and PRs.
README install: gemini extensions install https://github.com/gemini-cli-extensions/security
Apache-2.0 license listed on the repo; topics include gemini-cli-extensions and security.
Listed repeatedly in Piebald-AI/awesome-gemini-cli-extensions README.
uncertainty: Runtime accuracy of vulnerability findings versus traditional SAST was not independently verified.
Exact latest release date and ongoing issue volume were not fully enumerated.
aiReview.tagline: Gemini CLI commands to scan diffs and dependencies
aiReview.description: Adds Gemini CLI commands that review code changes and pull requests for security issues and scan dependencies via OSV-Scanner.
pros: Apache-2.0 GitHub repo under gemini-cli-extensions with README, changelog, contributing, and a security policy.
Documents /security:analyze on git diffs (default merge-base vs origin/HEAD) with optional JSON output and natural-language scope.
Documents /security:scan-deps using Google OSV-Scanner and OSV.dev, plus a sample GitHub Actions workflow with run-gemini-cli.
About 795 stars, 59 forks, 218 commits, and an mcp-server plus commands/skills layout.
cons: README states reports are a first-pass analysis, not a complete security audit.
Non-interactive /security:analyze is not supported yet (issue #20).
Requires Gemini CLI v0.4.0 or newer and a Gemini-backed workflow.

aiReview.summary: Official Apache-2.0 Gemini CLI extension that delegates background coding tasks (bugs, refactors, dependency updates) to Google’s Jules agent via /jules, with GitHub repo connection required.
evidence: Repo description and README: Gemini CLI extension orchestrating Jules for bug fixing, refactoring, dependency updates.
License Apache-2.0; topics gemini-cli-extensions; org gemini-cli-extensions.
Install command and /jules examples in README; 413 stars, 51 forks, 14 commits.
uncertainty: Jules backend pricing and quotas are not specified in the extension README.
Maintenance cadence beyond 14 commits and lack of tagged releases is unclear.
Runtime security of the MCP server and sudo npm install path not audited here.
aiReview.tagline: Delegate background coding tasks from Gemini CLI
aiReview.description: Install a Gemini CLI extension to offload bug fixes, refactors, and dependency updates to an async agent that can push GitHub branches.
pros: Public GitHub repo with Apache-2.0 license, README, CONTRIBUTING, and CI workflows.
Documents install via gemini extensions, /jules usage, and prerequisites including a Jules account and connected GitHub repo.
About 413 stars and 51 forks; listed on an awesome Gemini CLI extensions README.
Ships commands, mcp-server, gemini-extension.json, and GEMINI.md.
cons: Requires Gemini CLI v0.4.0+, a Jules account, and a GitHub repo connected to Jules.
Only 14 commits and no GitHub Releases listed.
May prompt for sudo to install Jules CLI via npm.

aiReview.summary: GitHub-backed Gemini CLI extension that bootstraps, modifies, tests, and commits Flutter/Dart work via slash commands. Experimental, Gemini CLI 0.4+ plus Flutter SDK required; fits a CLI-productivity list if the directory covers Gemini extensions.
evidence: https://github.com/gemini-cli-extensions/flutter README: Flutter extension for Gemini CLI; Status Experimental.
Install: gemini extensions install https://github.com/gemini-cli-extensions/flutter.git --auto-update
License BSD-3-Clause; ~401 stars, 27 forks, 75 commits on main.
Listed from Piebald-AI/awesome-gemini-cli-extensions curated README.
uncertainty: Release cadence and maintenance beyond README/commit count not independently verified.
Command behavior quality vs. advertised workflow not executed.
Windows install issue status beyond linked gemini-cli issue 10616.
aiReview.tagline: Slash commands to bootstrap and ship Flutter apps
aiReview.description: Install a Gemini CLI extension that creates Flutter projects, plans changes, runs pre-commit checks, and writes conventional commits.
pros: Public GitHub repo with README, BSD-3-Clause license, CHANGELOG, contributing guide, and 75 commits.
Documents install/update/uninstall via gemini extensions and lists /create-app, /create-package, /modify, and /commit.
Hundreds of stars and tens of forks indicate real usage for a Gemini CLI extension.
States prerequisites (Gemini CLI 0.4.0+, Flutter/Dart SDK, Git) and a Windows install workaround.
cons: README marks the project experimental and says features and commands may change drastically.
GitHub About has no description, website, or topics.
Depends on Gemini CLI rather than being a standalone terminal utility.

aiReview.summary: Deprecated Gemini CLI Firebase extension repo that now only points users to firebase/agent-skills; not a maintained CLI to list as a primary entry.
evidence: README title: Firebase Extension for Gemini CLI (Deprecated).
Replacement: gemini extensions install https://github.com/firebase/agent-skills.
GitHub: Apache-2.0, 124 stars, 19 forks, 13 commits, no About description.
uncertainty: Whether firebase/agent-skills is the listing that should replace this candidate.
Current maintenance status of the successor repo was not reviewed in depth.
aiReview.tagline: Deprecated Gemini CLI Firebase skills installer
aiReview.description: Install Firebase agent skills for Gemini CLI via a successor GitHub repo; this listing itself is deprecated.
pros: Public GitHub repo under Apache-2.0 with a short README.
README clearly states deprecation and the replacement install command.
cons: Repository is explicitly deprecated and replaced by firebase/agent-skills.
No GitHub description, topics, or website; only LICENSE and README remain.
13 commits and modest stars; not an independently maintained CLI.

aiReview.summary: Google Cloud-backed Gemini/Antigravity (and Claude Code/Codex) plugin that wraps MCP Toolbox’s Firestore server so agents can query and manage Firestore in natural language. Still beta (pre-v1.0), needs GCP credentials and IAM, and the listed GitHub org URL redirects to GoogleCloudPlatform/firestore-native-plugin.
evidence: GitHub About: “Skills for Firestore”; topics include gemini-cli-extension, mcp-related agent tooling.
README: packages MCP Toolbox prebuilt firestore server; tools for collections/documents; FIRESTORE_PROJECT / FIRESTORE_DATABASE.
License Apache-2.0; public GoogleCloudPlatform/firestore-native-plugin; ~30 stars, 6 forks.
Discovered repeatedly from Piebald-AI/awesome-gemini-cli-extensions.
uncertainty: Exact latest release version and install command freshness vs Gemini CLI vs Antigravity migration.
Runtime security of MCP Toolbox Firestore operations against production databases was not audited here.
Whether gemini-cli-extensions/firestore-native remains a stable canonical URL long-term.
aiReview.tagline: Agent plugin to query and manage Firestore via MCP
aiReview.description: Packages MCP Toolbox’s Firestore server as an agent plugin so you can inspect schemas, query data, and manage documents from CLI agents.
pros: Official GoogleCloudPlatform repo with Apache-2.0 license, changelog, contributing docs, and 122 commits.
Installs as a Gemini CLI / Antigravity plugin and also documents Claude Code and Codex support.
Documents prerequisites, ADC, IAM roles, env vars, and a list of Firestore tools plus a video walkthrough.
Listed on a curated awesome-gemini-cli-extensions README.
cons: README states it is beta (pre-v1.0) and may break until a stable release.
Requires Node/npx, a GCP project with Firestore enabled, Application Default Credentials, and specific IAM roles.
The candidate URL gemini-cli-extensions/firestore-native redirects to a different GitHub org/repo name.
Star count is modest (~30) so community adoption is still limited.

aiReview.summary: Official-style Gemini CLI extension that installs the gcloud MCP server so agents can run restricted gcloud commands. Preview wrapper with few commits; useful for Gemini CLI users, not a standalone CLI.
evidence: github.com/gemini-cli-extensions/gcloud README: Gemini CLI extension wrapping gcloud MCP
64 stars, 6 forks, Apache-2.0, 3 commits on main
gemini extensions install https://github.com/gemini-cli-extensions/gcloud
Tool table lists run_gcloud_command; denied-command list in gcloud-mcp
uncertainty: Maintenance cadence beyond three commits
Exact denied-command coverage over time
Whether this org is Google-staffed vs community
aiReview.tagline: Gemini CLI MCP bridge for Google Cloud gcloud
aiReview.description: Installs an MCP server so Gemini CLI can run restricted gcloud commands against your Google Cloud account.
pros: Apache-2.0 GitHub repo with README, contributing, and security policy.
Installs via gemini extensions install and exposes run_gcloud_command.
Documents denied commands and least-privilege impersonation.
Listed in awesome-gemini-cli-extensions.
cons: README states the repo is preview and not an officially supported Google product.
Only three commits and modest stars; implementation lives mainly in googleapis/gcloud-mcp.
Agent-run gcloud inherits the active account’s cloud permissions.

aiReview.summary: Official-style Gemini CLI extension that installs Genkit docs and MCP tools so the CLI can inspect, author, and debug Genkit apps. Small Apache-2.0 repo with modest stars and little extra documentation beyond install/usage examples.
evidence: README title: Genkit Extension for Gemini CLI; install URL matches canonical GitHub repo.
Apache-2.0 license badge and LICENSE file on the repo.
Stars 176, forks 19, 13 commits as shown on the GitHub page.
uncertainty: Cannot verify MCP tool surface, security of tools, or maintenance cadence beyond the landing page.
Organization relationship to Google/Genkit is not confirmed from About metadata.
aiReview.tagline: Gemini CLI tools and docs for Genkit apps
aiReview.description: Install a Gemini CLI extension that adds Genkit documentation and MCP tools to create, evaluate, and debug flows.
pros: README documents install via gemini extensions install and npx/Gemini CLI prerequisites.
Usage examples cover writing flows, evaluators, and analyzing traces.
Apache-2.0 license, contributing notes, and a gemini-extension.json manifest are present.
Public GitHub project with 176 stars, 19 forks, and 13 commits on main.
cons: GitHub About has no description, website, or topics.
Repo is small (docs plus a few root files) with no releases listed on the landing page.

aiReview.summary: Gemini CLI extension that wraps MCP Toolbox so you can define tools in tools.yaml and invoke them from the terminal; it is beta (pre-v1.0) and depends on Gemini CLI v0.6+ plus DB/cloud credentials.
evidence: README title Gemini CLI Extension - MCP Toolbox; install via gemini extensions install https://github.com/GoogleCloudPlatform/mcp-toolbox-plugin.
Public repo: Apache-2.0, ~109 stars, 10 forks, gemini-extension.json present.
Listed from Piebald-AI/awesome-gemini-cli-extensions as MCP Toolbox.
uncertainty: Runtime quality of generated MCP tools and database connectors not independently verified.
Maintenance cadence after last commit date not confirmed from this snapshot.
aiReview.tagline: Query custom MCP tools from Gemini CLI
aiReview.description: Install a Gemini CLI extension that loads MCP Toolbox, then invoke custom tools from tools.yaml with natural language in the terminal.
pros: Official GoogleCloudPlatform repo with Apache-2.0 license, changelog, contributing docs, and 99 commits.
Installs as a Gemini CLI extension and documents tools.yaml plus ADC for Google Cloud databases.
README includes troubleshooting for credentials, MCP connection, and binary download issues.
cons: Marked beta/pre-v1.0 with possible breaking changes until a stable release.
Requires Gemini CLI v0.6+, working ADC, and a local tools.yaml; GitHub listing has no About description.
Canonical listing URL gemini-cli-extensions/mcp-toolbox redirects to GoogleCloudPlatform/mcp-toolbox-plugin.

aiReview.summary: GitHub-backed Gemini CLI extension that talks to Neo4j via env-configured credentials, exposing schema listing and Cypher execution through natural-language prompts. Beta, few stars, and install docs point at a different org URL than this repo.
evidence: GitHub about: Neo4j extension for Gemini-CLI; Apache-2.0 license.
Listed as Neo4j in Piebald-AI/awesome-gemini-cli-extensions.
README tools: list_tables and execute_cypher; NEO4J_URI/USER/PASSWORD required.
uncertainty: Whether this repo is the canonical extension versus gemini-cli-extensions/neo4j.
Runtime security of execute_cypher against a live database was not audited.
Maintenance cadence beyond 5 commits is unverified.
aiReview.tagline: Query Neo4j from Gemini CLI with Cypher tools
aiReview.description: Adds Neo4j schema listing and Cypher execution to Gemini CLI so you can explore graphs and generate code from natural-language prompts.
pros: Apache-2.0 GitHub repo with README covering install, env vars, tools, and usage examples.
Documents two tools: list_tables for schema and execute_cypher for queries.
Requires Gemini CLI v0.6.0+, a running Neo4j instance, and database credentials via environment variables.
cons: README states the extension is beta (pre-v1.0) and may break until 1.0.
Repository shows 3 stars, 0 forks, and 5 commits, so community traction is low.
Install command targets github.com/gemini-cli-extensions/neo4j, not this canonical URL.

aiReview.summary: Official Google Cloud plugin that wraps MCP Toolbox’s AlloyDB for PostgreSQL server so agents can manage clusters, run SQL, and inspect schemas via env-configured credentials. Beta (pre-v1.0) with modest stars; useful if you already run AlloyDB and an MCP-capable CLI agent.
evidence: canonicalUrl github.com/gemini-cli-extensions/alloydb redirects to GoogleCloudPlatform/alloydb-plugin; README describes MCP Toolbox alloydb-postgres packaging.
Listed repeatedly in Piebald-AI/awesome-gemini-cli-extensions.
Topics include gemini-cli-extension, mcp, claude-code, codex; Apache-2.0 and beta note in README.
Releases still referenced at gemini-cli-extensions/alloydb.
uncertainty: Exact latest release version and toolbox pin in mcp.json were not re-verified beyond README.
Runtime safety of MCP SQL/admin tools against production clusters was not tested.
aiReview.tagline: Agent plugin for AlloyDB Postgres via MCP Toolbox
aiReview.description: Install an MCP plugin so AI agents can provision AlloyDB, query Postgres, explore schemas, and monitor clusters with GCP credentials.
pros: GoogleCloudPlatform repo packages MCP Toolbox’s prebuilt alloydb-postgres server as an Agent Plugins v1 extension.
Documents install paths for Antigravity/Gemini CLI, Claude Code, Codex, and other compatible clients, plus required env vars and IAM roles.
Apache-2.0 license, changelog, contributing docs, evals, and 128 commits on main.
Toolsets cover admin, access, data/SQL, monitor, health, optimize, and replication workflows.
cons: README states the project is beta (pre-v1.0) and may break until a stable release.
GitHub popularity is low (about 24 stars and 6 forks at review time).
Needs Node/npx, ADC, AlloyDB API, and matching VPC for private IP; agents can run admin and SQL operations.

aiReview.summary: Official Gemini CLI / agent plugin that wraps MCP Toolbox’s prebuilt Spanner server so agents can query schemas and data via natural language. Beta (pre-v1.0), Apache-2.0, modest GitHub traction; requires GCP credentials and a supported agent.
evidence: GitHub description: Gemini CLI extension / skills for interacting with Cloud Spanner via MCP Toolbox.
License Apache-2.0; topics include gemini-cli-extension.
README lists SPANNER_PROJECT/INSTANCE/DATABASE, databaseReader/databaseUser IAM, and agent version floors.
uncertainty: Exact latest release quality and MCP tool surface not fully enumerated here.
Canonical URL vs GoogleCloudPlatform/spanner-plugin redirect/rename.
Runtime security of execute-SQL tools against production Spanner.
aiReview.tagline: Agent plugin for Spanner queries, schemas, and DB ops
aiReview.description: Packages MCP Toolbox’s Spanner server so Gemini CLI and other agents can manage databases, run SQL, and inspect schemas with natural language.
pros: Apache-2.0 repo under gemini-cli-extensions / GoogleCloudPlatform with changelog, contributing docs, and 100+ commits.
Documents install for Gemini/Antigravity, Claude Code, and Codex plus env vars and IAM roles.
Listed in a curated Gemini CLI extensions README and referenced from Google Cloud Spanner MCP docs.
cons: README states beta/pre-v1.0 with possible breaking changes.
Low public adoption (about 19 stars and 3 forks).
Needs Node/npx, ADC, and Spanner IAM; not a standalone CLI.

aiReview.summary: Official Google Cloud plugin that wraps MCP Toolbox’s Cloud SQL for MySQL server so Gemini CLI and similar agents can manage instances, schemas, and queries. It is Apache-2.0, actively documented, still beta, and needs GCP credentials plus a compatible agent.
evidence: GitHub about: Skills for Cloud SQL for MySQL; Apache-2.0; topics include gemini-cli-extension.
README: beta note, MCP Toolbox packaging, env vars CLOUD_SQL_MYSQL_*, IAM roles, Node/npx MCP server.
Listed in Piebald-AI/awesome-gemini-cli-extensions as Google Cloud SQL for MySQL.
uncertainty: Exact latest release quality and eval coverage not independently run.
Ongoing maintenance cadence beyond commit count and docs not verified.
aiReview.tagline: Agent plugin for Cloud SQL MySQL via MCP Toolbox
aiReview.description: Install an MCP-backed plugin so agents can manage Cloud SQL MySQL instances, explore schemas, and run queries with GCP credentials.
pros: Apache-2.0 repo under GoogleCloudPlatform with README, changelog, contributing docs, and 115 commits.
Packages MCP Toolbox’s prebuilt cloud-sql-mysql server for Gemini CLI, Claude Code, Codex, and Antigravity.
Documents env vars, IAM roles, ADC, IP types, and install commands for supported agents.
cons: README states the project is beta (pre-v1.0) and may break until a stable release.
Only 12 stars and 2 forks; usage is limited to users with Cloud SQL and a supported agent.
Canonical gemini-cli-extensions URL redirects to GoogleCloudPlatform/cloud-sql-mysql-plugin.

aiReview.summary: Official Google Cloud plugin that wraps MCP Toolbox’s Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL server so Gemini CLI, Claude Code, Codex, and Antigravity can manage instances and query data via natural language. It is still beta (pre-v1.0) and needs GCP credentials, IAM, and a compatible agent.
evidence: GitHub About: Skills for Cloud SQL for PostgreSQL; topics include gemini-cli-extension and mcp.
README: packages MCP Toolbox prebuilt cloud-sql-postgres server; beta note; Apache-2.0.
gemini-extension.json, mcp.json, plugin.json present in repo file listing.
Source listing in Piebald-AI/awesome-gemini-cli-extensions.
uncertainty: Runtime security of MCP tools executing against production databases was not audited.
Release cadence and v1.0 timeline not verified beyond beta disclaimer.
Exact star/activity numbers may change; page showed 42 stars and 7 forks.
aiReview.tagline: Agent plugin for Cloud SQL PostgreSQL via MCP
aiReview.description: Package MCP Toolbox’s Cloud SQL Postgres server as an AI agent plugin to manage instances, schemas, and queries in natural language.
pros: GoogleCloudPlatform-maintained repo with Apache-2.0 license, changelog, contributing docs, and 156 commits.
Installs as a Gemini CLI / Antigravity / Claude Code / Codex plugin wrapping a documented MCP Toolbox server.
Documents env vars, IAM roles, ADC, and private-IP networking requirements.
Listed in the awesome-gemini-cli-extensions curated README.
cons: README states beta (pre-v1.0) with possible breaking changes.
Requires a supported AI agent, Node.js/npx, enabled Cloud SQL Admin API, and GCP IAM.
Canonical URL gemini-cli-extensions/cloud-sql-postgresql redirects to GoogleCloudPlatform/cloud-sql-postgresql-plugin.
Low star count (~42) relative to typical CLI utilities.

aiReview.tagline: Unauthenticated MCP to search a public AI-tools catalog
aiReview.description: Query a curated AI-tools catalog over MCP: search, fetch, compare, and find alternatives from Claude, Cursor, or any MCP client.
pros: Documents five read-only MCP tools plus Claude Code, HTTP, and stdio/mcp-remote setup.
Endpoint is unauthenticated and free; limits (read-only, POST-only, catalog freshness) are stated on the page.
Results expose sponsored and verified flags, and compare/alternatives handle unmatched names explicitly.
cons: Listing comes from a commercial directory with UTM referral tracking, not a GitHub-backed CLI.
Catalog pricing and features are build-time records, not live vendor data.
No GitHub repo, license, or changelog is shown on the MCP page.

aiReview.summary: Comparison catalog of GTM/LinkedIn enrichment and scraper APIs, not a CLI or Gemini MCP server; listed URL does not document an MCP server.
evidence: Homepage: 'Datacircle is a sheet of GTM APIs' comparing LinkedIn profile and related APIs.
Candidate URL path /mcp-server fetched as datacircle.dev index, not MCP instructions.
Discovered only as a one-word link in Piebald-AI/awesome-gemini-cli.
FAQ: signup with work email for CSV/JSON/zip plus a 10 million U.S. B2B leads gift.
uncertainty: Whether an MCP server exists at all.
Accuracy and freshness of vendor pricing rows.
Legal status of listed scrapers and the leads gift.
aiReview.tagline: Compare GTM and LinkedIn enrichment API pricing
aiReview.description: Side-by-side sheets of LinkedIn, email, phone, and company APIs with cost, freshness, limits, and fields from vendor docs.
pros: Documents many GTM API categories with cost, freshness, rate limits, speed, and returned fields.
States numbers come from each provider’s pricing pages and docs, with source pages in the CSV.
Offers CSV, JSON, and zip downloads plus per-plan pages with llms.txt.
cons: Canonical MCP-server docs URL redirects to the marketing sheet, with no MCP setup shown.
It is a comparison spreadsheet, not a command-line or terminal utility.
Downloads require work-email signup; the site also advertises 10 million U.S. B2B leads.
Catalog centers LinkedIn scrapers and people-data APIs, which often conflict with platform terms.

aiReview.summary: Hosted MCP endpoint that exposes LinkedNav’s LinkedIn outreach workspace (lists, campaigns, enrichment, unibox) to Claude and other MCP clients via API key. Commercial sales-automation product, not a GitHub CLI; LinkedIn automation carries ToS and spam risk.
evidence: Page title and meta describe LinkedIn MCP for AI assistants; server URL and 7-day trial/signup CTAs.
awesome-gemini-cli README only lists the product name and UTM’d /mcp URL.
FAQ claims any streamable-HTTP MCP client, Bearer key, and credit usage matching the dashboard.
uncertainty: Actual tool count, reliability, and LinkedIn compliance cannot be verified from marketing copy.
Plan pricing and whether Gemini CLI works as well as Claude were not independently tested.
No source code or security audit of the MCP server.
aiReview.tagline: MCP access to LinkedIn outreach, lists, and enrichment
aiReview.description: Connect an MCP client with a URL and API key to search leads, run LinkedIn campaigns, enrich contacts, and query results in natural language.
pros: Documents a hosted MCP URL (https://mcp.linkednav.com) and Claude connector setup with API key auth.
Lists many workspace tools (campaigns, lists, enrichment, unibox, senders) with example natural-language prompts.
States MCP access is included in the plan; some sizing/signal queries are described as free.
Notes rate limits (300 rpm), workspace-scoped keys, and client confirmation before sends.
cons: Commercial LinkedIn outreach platform with trial/signup, not an open-source CLI.
No public GitHub repo, license, or independent changelog in the candidate facts.
LinkedIn campaign sending and account reconnect/2FA tools may conflict with LinkedIn terms of service.

aiReview.summary: Hosted LinkedIn MCP endpoint you paste into Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor, Claude Code, or n8n; not a GitHub CLI. Independent of LinkedIn and explicitly notes account-restriction risk from automated activity.
evidence: Page title and meta describe a hosted LinkedIn MCP server, free to start.
Pricing table: Free $0 (disconnect after idle), Connect $29.99/mo, Agent $499/mo.
FAQ: not official LinkedIn MCP; automation may violate LinkedIn terms.
Discovered as HeyReagent in Piebald-AI/awesome-gemini-cli README.
uncertainty: Could not verify GitHub source, uptime, or security of LinkedIn credential handling.
Could not independently verify action count, daily limits, or plan entitlements.
Gemini CLI compatibility is not documented on this page (Claude Code/Cursor are).
aiReview.tagline: Hosted MCP to read and act on your LinkedIn
aiReview.description: Paste one MCP URL so AI apps can read your inbox, message, invite, search, and post on your LinkedIn account.
pros: Documents a remote MCP URL (https://api.heyreagent.com/mcp) and setup for Claude, ChatGPT, Muse, Claude Code, Cursor, and n8n.
Lists 97 actions across profile, messages, search, posts, jobs, and related LinkedIn products, with per-action docs.
Publishes daily action caps, free vs paid connection behavior, and that it is unofficial and not affiliated with LinkedIn.
cons: Commercial hosted SaaS, not a maintained open-source CLI, which the CLI-directory rubric prefers.
Candidate URL includes referral UTM parameters rather than a clean canonical listing.
Site states LinkedIn’s User Agreement disallows automated activity and that accounts can still be restricted despite limits.

aiReview.summary: Official reference for Tern’s `tern plugin` subcommands (list, install, link, reload, types). Useful for Tern plugin authors; it is documentation of a product-specific CLI, not a standalone GitHub-backed tool.
evidence: Page title Command Line; synopsis lists `tern plugin list|reload|dir|install|remove|link|unlink|types`.
States it manages the plugins folder and asks the session daemon to reload; never runs plugin Lua.
Discovered from curated_readme theblazehen/awesome-tern as “Plugin CLI”.
Install SRC includes github.com/OWNER/REPO[/PATH] and git clone --depth 1.
uncertainty: Tern product pricing, license, and source-repo health.
Whether the CLI is distributed independently of the Tern app.
How widely used or maintained relative to other awesome-list CLIs.
aiReview.tagline: Manage, link, and reload local Tern plugins from the shell
aiReview.description: Install, link, list, and reload Tern plugins, clone git sources, and emit Luau type stubs without executing plugin Lua.
pros: Documents a full `tern plugin` surface: list, reload, dir, install, remove, link, unlink, and types.
Specifies flags, JSON output, exit codes (including daemon timeout 124), and error messages.
Install supports local paths and git/GitHub sources with `--force` and pre-copy manifest checks.
Link/unlink is described as a development workflow that watches the source directory without copying.
cons: The candidate URL is product documentation, not a standalone CLI repository.
The CLI is tied to the Tern session daemon and machine plugins folder; iOS has no CLI.
Maintenance, license, and GitHub activity for the CLI itself are not shown on this page.

aiReview.summary: GitHub client that wires coding-agent CLIs (including Gemini CLI) to a hosted long-term memory service via hooks and MCP. Source-available with many adapters, but the repo is tiny (1 star), uses a non-standard license, and real storage/embeddings live on a third-party service.
evidence: Repo description and README: thin client for brethof-brain persistent agent memory; Gemini CLI extension among ~20 adapters.
Language Python; LICENSE Other; Stars 1; discovered from Piebald-AI/awesome-gemini-cli.
README states no third-party deps on the client and that embeddings/retrieval happen on the service.
uncertainty: Cannot verify hosted-service pricing, data retention, or production reliability.
Cannot verify claimed VM test-rig coverage for every listed platform.
Exact license terms beyond GitHub 'Other' were not fully audited.
aiReview.tagline: Hook/MCP client for persistent AI-agent memory
aiReview.description: Forwards coding-agent hooks to a hosted memory service and exposes MCP tools for search and save across many CLI harnesses.
pros: README documents a full ambient loop (session brief, per-prompt recall, archival) plus MCP tools for many coding CLIs.
Includes a dedicated Gemini CLI adapter and is listed from awesome-gemini-cli.
Client claims Python 3.9+ stdlib-only core and per-adapter install READMEs.
Repository includes CI workflow and numerous adapter directories.
cons: GitHub stats are very low (1 star, 0 forks, 0 issues) so maintenance and community signal are weak.
License is listed as Other / source-available, not a standard OSI license.
Memory storage, embeddings, and retrieval run on an external hosted service requiring API keys.

aiReview.summary: Gemini CLI extension that talks to a hosted MCP social scheduler so you can draft, schedule, and publish posts across many networks after a browser login. Repo is MIT with skills and install docs but has no stars or issues and requires a paid plan or trial.
evidence: GitHub description and README: write, schedule, publish to Instagram, TikTok, YouTube, LinkedIn, X and more; hosted MCP, no API key.
Install: gemini extensions install https://github.com/posteverywhere/gemini-cli-extension
MCP at https://mcp.posteverywhere.ai/mcp; pricing link for plan or trial.
MIT License listed on the repo.
uncertainty: Cannot verify MCP uptime, actual tool behavior, or account billing without using the service.
Cannot verify maintenance cadence beyond a snapshot with zero community metrics.
aiReview.tagline: Schedule social posts from Gemini CLI via hosted MCP
aiReview.description: Install a Gemini CLI extension that drafts, schedules, and publishes posts across major networks using a hosted MCP after browser sign-in.
pros: README documents gemini extensions install, browser OAuth, and the hosted MCP URL.
Repository includes gemini-extension.json, GEMINI.md, and 15 skill files covering schedule, calendar, analytics, and failed-post retry.
License is MIT; plugin is described as instructions plus MCP address with no local runtime code.
cons: GitHub shows 0 stars, 0 forks, and 0 issues.
Using the tools requires a PostEverywhere account with a plan or active free trial.
Publishing depends on a third-party hosted MCP rather than a self-contained CLI.

aiReview.summary: SaaS CI platform with an MCP server so coding agents can pull failure bundles, triage runs, and optionally re-run workflows or start billed one-off jobs. The listed URL is product documentation, not a standalone CLI.
evidence: Source listing: Piebald-AI/awesome-gemini-cli README anchor Latchkey.
Docs describe 11 MCP tools plus fix/triage prompt flows and lk_live_ keys.
Jobs billed as runner minutes; AI Insight shortcut keys expire in 90 days and can run jobs.
uncertainty: Exact paid vs free-minute limits and GitHub org/repo health.
Whether Gemini CLI is first-class vs generic MCP HTTP clients.
aiReview.tagline: MCP access to CI failures, logs, and opt-in job runs
aiReview.description: Connect MCP agents to workspace-scoped CI failure data, with optional workflow dispatch and billed one-off runners.
pros: Documents an HTTP MCP server at latchkey.dev/mcp with API keys and Claude Code/Cursor setup.
Default keys are read-only and workspace-scoped; dispatch and job-run scopes are explicit opt-ins.
Failure bundles include logs, diagnosis, and self-healing context; secrets are described as scrubbed.
Publishes OpenAPI, MCP manifest, agent.txt, and markdown twins of docs pages.
cons: Candidate is a marketing/docs URL with UTM params, not a GitHub-backed CLI.
Write-capable keys can dispatch workflows or spend runner minutes if leaked.
Pricing and GitHub maintenance of a public CLI cannot be confirmed from this page alone.

aiReview.summary: Third-party 2026 explainer of Gemini CLI quotas and API-key token prices, citing Google docs and noting unverified Code Assist seat prices. Useful as a pricing reference, not a CLI or SDK.
evidence: Page title and meta describe Gemini CLI limits 2026: 1,500/2,000 requests per day, free tier and API cost.
Usage limits section: 1,500 req/user/day Standard, 2,000 Enterprise; personal 1,000/day tier reported discontinued June 18, 2026.
API price table lists models with $/1M input/cached/output and source https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/pricing.
Discovered from Piebald-AI/awesome-gemini-cli README as “Gemini CLI limits & pricing (QuotaBurn).”
uncertainty: Cannot independently confirm 2026 model names, scheduled price doubles, or free-tier discontinuation against live Google docs in this review.
Site traffic, authorship, and update cadence beyond the stated verification date are unknown.
Accuracy of “default workload” monthly cost estimates (~$17–$100) is not audited.
aiReview.tagline: Gemini CLI quotas, plans, and API token prices
aiReview.description: Summarizes Gemini CLI daily request quotas, Code Assist vs API-key billing, and per-model token rates with dated source links.
pros: States verification date (2026-10-13) and links Google quota and Gemini API pricing docs.
Explains that Gemini CLI counts model requests, not prompts, and that one prompt can consume several requests.
Documents Standard (1,500) and Enterprise (2,000) daily shared quotas with Code Assist agent mode.
Marks Code Assist seat prices as unverified rather than inventing numbers.
cons: It is a marketing/content site (QuotaBurn) with referral UTM and an email list, not an official Google page.
Code Assist Standard and Enterprise monthly seat prices are left blank.
Free-tier discontinuation is described as reported, while the official README may still advertise it.

aiReview.summary: Official Google Antigravity docs for the /btw slash command: ephemeral side questions that inherit session context without tools or growing main history. Useful as a command reference, not a standalone CLI product.
evidence: Page title and URL are Antigravity docs: Side question command (/btw).
Documents /btw in App and CLI, copy via /copy btw, and unavailable in headless -p/--print.
Rubric prefers GitHub-backed CLIs; this candidate is official web documentation for one slash command.
uncertainty: Cannot verify product pricing, open-source status, or CLI maintenance from this page alone.
Cannot verify runtime quality of the /btw implementation beyond the docs.
aiReview.tagline: Ephemeral side questions without growing chat history
aiReview.description: Ask a one-turn contextual question while an agent turn runs; answers skip tools and are not stored in main conversation history.
pros: Official documentation with concrete CLI usage, notes, and keyboard shortcuts.
Describes behavior clearly: context inheritance, no tools, no main-history growth, and in-flight limits.
Links related slash commands and CLI reference pages.
States headless-mode limitation explicitly.
cons: This is a single-command docs page, not a standalone maintained CLI repository.
Requires the Antigravity app or CLI; the page is not a downloadable tool.
No GitHub source, version history, or license for the command itself.

aiReview.summary: Official docs for the Antigravity CLI `/changelog` slash command (TUI viewer, cache, headless/JSON print). A single-command page, not a standalone tool listing.
evidence: Page documents `/changelog` fetching notes to ~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/cache/CHANGELOG.md.
Lists keyboard navigation and `agy -p "/changelog" --output-format json`.
Source is official antigravity.google docs, not a curated CLI repo.
uncertainty: Cannot verify CLI maintenance, license, or GitHub presence from this page alone.
Pricing of Antigravity product beyond this free docs page is unknown.
aiReview.tagline: Terminal viewer for versioned CLI release notes
aiReview.description: Open scrollable Antigravity CLI release notes in-session, or print Markdown/JSON from cache or the agy binary.
pros: Official Google Antigravity docs describe `/changelog` with TUI keys, cache path, and offline fallback.
Documents headless print via `agy -p "/changelog"`, JSON output, and `agy changelog`.
Links to install/update, web changelog, and CLI reference.
cons: Candidate is a subcommand doc page, not a GitHub-backed CLI or full product entry.
Title is a slash-command label, weak as a directory listing.
Depends on the Antigravity/`agy` CLI; no independent install surface here.

aiReview.summary: Official docs for the Antigravity CLI /context slash command, which inspects token use, compaction checkpoints, and tracked files. Useful as CLI reference, but it is a single-command page rather than a standalone tool listing.
evidence: Page title and overview describe /context as opening an interactive Context Usage panel in the Antigravity CLI.
Docs list token categories, visual grid markers, checkpoint/file sections, and navigation keys.
Discovered from official antigravity.google docs; no risk flags on the candidate record.
uncertainty: Could not verify CLI license, pricing, GitHub maintenance, or whether the command exists outside this product.
No independent runtime verification of the panel behavior.
aiReview.tagline: Inspect CLI context-window usage and token breakdown
aiReview.description: Open a terminal panel that shows context-window occupancy, token categories, checkpoints, and tracked files for the active CLI session.
pros: Official documentation with concrete slash-command usage, panel layout, and keyboard shortcuts.
Explains token categories, compaction checkpoints, and related commands such as /btw, /clear, /fork, and /rewind.
Includes practical guidance for keeping long sessions within model context limits.
cons: The URL is a single-command doc page, not a standalone CLI project or downloadable tool.
Requires the Antigravity CLI environment; the page does not document installation or licensing.

aiReview.summary: Official Antigravity CLI docs for the /effort slash command, which sets model reasoning budget (low through max) interactively, by argument, or via --effort in headless mode. Useful as CLI reference, not a standalone tool.
evidence: Page title and overview describe /effort as controlling thinking budget for the selected model in Antigravity CLI.
Lists levels low/medium/high/xhigh/max, interactive gauge keys, argument form, and agy -p / --effort headless behavior.
Canonical URL is antigravity.google docs, not a GitHub CLI repository.
uncertainty: Could not verify CLI availability, license, pricing, or maintenance outside this docs page.
Facts payload was empty; content taken from the published markdown docs.
aiReview.tagline: Set CLI model reasoning budget per session or run
aiReview.description: Documented slash command and --effort flag to pick low–max reasoning tiers, persist defaults, and inspect effort in headless CLI runs.
pros: Official command reference covering interactive picker, direct arguments, and headless inspect/override.
Documents effort tiers (low, medium, high, xhigh, max) and model-specific availability.
Includes validation messages, keybindings, and distinction between persisted /effort and one-shot --effort.
cons: Single slash-command page, not a standalone CLI product or GitHub-backed utility.
Requires the Antigravity CLI and models that expose adjustable effort; not independently usable.

aiReview.summary: Apache-2.0 TypeScript terminal coding agent with multi-provider support, plan-before-edit flow, and Homebrew/npm install. Flag the installer: it silently replaces any PATH `agent` binary, plus optional computer-use and trace upload.
evidence: README: open-source terminal coding agent, 15+ providers, plan mode, Claude Code import.
Repo metadata: TypeScript, Apache License 2.0, ~206 stars, 37 forks, 40 issues.
README documents Homebrew, curl|bash, PATH `agent` replacement, ahtraces, and computer-use MCP.
uncertainty: Cannot independently verify release cadence, security review of install scripts, or commercial vs free API usage.
COMMERCIAL.md exists but was not fully reviewed for paid-tier terms.
aiReview.tagline: Terminal AI agent that plans, edits, and runs tools
aiReview.description: Run a terminal-native coding agent with multi-provider models, plan mode, skills, and approval before risky edits.
pros: GitHub-backed TypeScript CLI with Apache-2.0 license, CI workflows, and extensive docs.
Supports interactive REPL, prompt mode, multiple model providers including local models, and git-aware workflows.
Installable via Homebrew, curl script, npm, or building from source with Bun.
cons: Installers scan writable PATH directories and replace any existing `agent` command without a prompt.
Optional computer-use and local/cloud tracing increase privilege and telemetry surface.
Star count is modest (~200) relative to the size of the competing coding-agent CLI space.

aiReview.summary: Official ClickHouse agent-skills repo with packaged best-practice, architecture, JS troubleshooting, and chdb skills for coding agents; GitHub-backed Apache-2.0 docs, not a standalone CLI.
evidence: GitHub description: The official Agent Skills for ClickHouse and ClickHouse Cloud.
README lists npx and clickhousectl install, five skill areas, Apache-2.0, 40 commits.
Discovered from heilcheng/awesome-agent-skills curated README.
uncertainty: Skill completeness and accuracy versus current ClickHouse versions not independently verified.
Maintenance cadence beyond 40 commits and star/fork counts not audited.
aiReview.tagline: Official agent skills for ClickHouse and chdb
aiReview.description: Install packaged agent skills covering ClickHouse schema, queries, architecture, Node client troubleshooting, and in-process chdb APIs.
pros: Official ClickHouse org repo with Apache-2.0 license, README, and ~550 stars.
Documents multiple skills: best practices (28 rules), architecture advisor, Node.js client troubleshooting, and chdb.
Install paths include npx skills add clickhouse/agent-skills and clickhousectl skills.
Skills follow the agentskills.io specification and include human-readable SKILL.md/AGENTS.md.
cons: It is instruction packs for AI agents, not a command-line productivity utility.
Source listing title clickhouse/clickhouse-best-practices does not match the repo name agent-skills.

aiReview.summary: Official Google Workspace org CLI (`gws`) that dynamically maps Discovery APIs for Drive, Gmail, Calendar, and related services, with OAuth setup, JSON output, and bundled agent skills. Strong GitHub-backed CLI fit; note it is not an officially supported Google product and is pre-v1 with expected breaking changes.
evidence: https://github.com/googleworkspace/cli README: gws, Discovery Service, npm @googleworkspace/cli, Apache-2.0, not officially supported.
Repo topics include cli, google-workspace, oauth2, rust, agent-skills; languages/crates plus skills/ and gemini-extension.json.
Stars ~31.7k, forks ~2k, CI badge, Node 18+ or binary installs, brew install googleworkspace-cli.
uncertainty: Exact current release version and long-term API stability toward v1.0.
Whether all Workspace APIs/scopes work equally for consumer vs Workspace admin accounts.
aiReview.tagline: Dynamic CLI for Workspace APIs and agent skills
aiReview.description: Call Drive, Gmail, Calendar, Sheets, Docs, Chat, and Admin from one CLI built from Discovery, with OAuth, JSON output, and agent skills.
pros: Apache-2.0 GitHub repo under googleworkspace with CI, changelog, security policy, and install via npm, Homebrew, cargo, Nix, and releases.
Commands are generated at runtime from Google Discovery Service rather than a fixed command list.
Includes OAuth setup/login, structured JSON, dry-run, pagination, and 40+ agent skills plus a Gemini CLI extension.
Large public activity (~31.7k stars, ~2k forks, 283 commits) and multiple install paths including prebuilt binaries.
cons: README states it is not an officially supported Google product and is under active development with breaking changes before v1.0.
Requires a Google Cloud project and OAuth credentials plus a Workspace-capable Google account.
Source listing used the name gws-workflow while the repo is googleworkspace/cli.

aiReview.summary: GitHub-backed MIT CLI that launches many tools via npx with JSON-first output and skill search, aimed at humans and agents. High commit volume and docs, but star count is modest relative to 10k+ tool claims.
evidence: Repo description: 10,000+ CLI tools, one CLI, zero configuration.
README: npx supercli skills search/get and JSON default with --human.
Topics: agents, cli, harness, skills; MIT license; site javimosch.github.io/supercli.
uncertainty: Whether 10,000 plugins are independently maintained and safe to execute.
npm package health, runtime security of remote tool execution, and current release cadence.
aiReview.tagline: JSON-first launcher for thousands of CLI tools
aiReview.description: Run and discover thousands of CLIs, APIs, and workflows through one npx command with JSON-first output and no local installs.
pros: Public MIT-licensed GitHub repo with README, tests, CI workflows, and 2,439 commits.
Installs via npx supercli with skill search/get and JSON-first execution examples.
Documents agent-oriented usage, plugins, and a claimed 10k+ plugin catalog.
cons: Only 54 stars and 6 forks, so adoption is still small versus the catalog size claimed.
Marketing-heavy README and large generated plugin/marketing trees make independent quality of all tools hard to verify.

aiReview.summary: MIT-licensed Agent Skills package with a 98-rule design spec and audit protocol for agent-safe CLIs. It is documentation/skill content, not a command-line app, and has very little GitHub traction.
evidence: GitHub description and README: AI-native CLI design spec, 98 rules, Agent Skills compatible.
Repo has SKILL.md and references/audit.md, MIT license, 25 commits, 3 stars, 0 forks.
uncertainty: Rule quality and completeness were not audited line-by-line.
Maintenance beyond recent commits and real-world adoption are unknown.
aiReview.tagline: 98-rule spec for agent-safe CLI design
aiReview.description: Defines JSON output, errors, contracts, and exit codes so agents can call CLIs reliably. Ships as an Agent Skills package with an audit protocol.
pros: README documents 98 rules across 11 dimensions plus an audit protocol.
MIT license and install paths for Claude Code and OpenAI Codex skills.
Certification levels (Agent-Friendly / Ready / Native) are spelled out.
cons: Not a CLI or terminal utility; it is a spec/skill for building CLIs.
Very low adoption (3 stars, 0 forks) as of the review snapshot.
Claims of 30+ agent compatibility are not independently verified here.

aiReview.summary: Maintained TypeScript/Bun CLI for Google Sheets with JSON output, key-based updates, and agent skill files; install is clone-and-build rather than a published package.
evidence: Repo description: Composable Google Sheets CLI for humans and agents; read/write/update cells by key with Agent Skills.
package.json version 1.0.2, license MIT, bin sheets-cli, dependencies commander and googleapis.
README documents OAuth login, SHEETS_CLI_DEFAULT_SPREADSHEET_ID, and example read/update commands.
Discovered from heilcheng/awesome-agent-skills curated README.
uncertainty: Test coverage and CI pass status not verified beyond scripts existing.
Token storage security and OAuth localhost flow not audited.
Whether the binary is published to npm despite bin field is unverified.
aiReview.tagline: JSON Google Sheets CLI for humans and agents
aiReview.description: Read, append, and update Google Sheets from the terminal with JSON output, OAuth, and agent skill files for coding agents.
pros: Public GitHub repo with documented commands for read, append, key-based update, auth, and JSON output.
MIT-licensed TypeScript project using Commander and the official googleapis client, with lint/test/build scripts.
Includes SKILL.md, AGENTS.md, and CLAUDE.md for Claude Code and OpenAI Codex.
Recent activity (about 20 commits) and modest adoption (~70 stars, 6 forks).
cons: Installation is git clone plus bun install/build; no npm/Homebrew distribution is documented.
Requires Bun, Google Cloud OAuth desktop credentials, and Sheets/Drive APIs.
Star count and commit history are still small relative to long-lived Sheets CLIs.

aiReview.summary: Commercial screenshot API with an MCP endpoint and agent-oriented docs; useful for AI agents but it is a hosted SaaS, not a GitHub-backed CLI, so it is a weak fit for a CLI-focused awesome list.
evidence: Docs describe JSON-RPC MCP tools/call for take_screenshot with url/format and quota remaining in the response.
pricing.md lists Free/Starter/Growth/Scale monthly screenshot quotas and overage.
Discovered from Piebald-AI/awesome-gemini-cli README as CurlShot, not as a local CLI.
uncertainty: GitHub MCP repo quality, license, and activity were not independently verified in this pass.
Uptime, abuse controls, and whether screenshots of arbitrary URLs raise ToS issues were not audited.
aiReview.tagline: Hosted API and MCP server for web page screenshots
aiReview.description: Render public pages to images, PDF, or scroll video via REST or MCP, with caching, quotas, and machine-readable docs for agents.
pros: Documents an MCP endpoint at https://curlshot.com/api/mcp with take_screenshot and list_devices.
Provides llms.txt, OpenAPI, markdown docs, and well-known MCP/API catalog files for agents.
Pricing is published: free 100 screenshots/month and paid plans from $19.
MCP setup notes point to a GitHub repo at SergiuPogor/curlshot-mcp.
cons: The listed URL is a product guide with UTM tracking, not an open-source CLI.
Screenshot capture consumes a paid quota and requires a Bearer access key.
Core product is a hosted service, so maintenance and availability are vendor-controlled.

aiReview.summary: MCP server, REST Agent API, and unpublished CLI for driving an SEO/content platform from AI agents, with public readiness tools and no agent publish path. Fits agent/CLI directories more than generic terminal utilities.
evidence: Docs page lists readiness tools (check_readiness, propose_schema, generate_machine_readable, readiness_report) and 22 scoped account tools.
Hosted MCP URL https://app.altorank.co/api/mcp with OAuth PKCE; self-host via claude mcp add and apps/web/scripts/mcp.ts.
FAQ states OSS self-host needs no paid plan; managed plans and hosted endpoint exist.
Discovered from Piebald-AI/awesome-gemini-cli README as AltoRank.
uncertainty: Repository license, star count, and maintenance cadence were not fetched.
Actual npm CLI package availability and Gemini CLI skill install quality were not verified.
Paid-plan limits beyond drafting quota were not enumerated.
aiReview.tagline: Agent MCP and API for SEO audits, keywords, and drafts
aiReview.description: Drive site readiness checks, keyword planning, and draft generation via 26 MCP tools, a scoped REST API, and a CLI. Agents cannot publish.
pros: Documents 26 MCP tools plus a REST Agent API and a CLI over the same routes.
Four readiness tools work against public domains without an API key.
Explicitly omits publish, approve, and delete from MCP, REST, and CLI.
Source is linked at github.com/AltoRank/altorank; self-host and hosted Streamable HTTP MCP are both described.
cons: The CLI is described as packaged for npm but not yet published.
Account tools, drafting quota, and the hosted endpoint depend on the commercial app and API keys.
Listing target is awesome-gemini-cli; this is an SEO product MCP more than a general shell utility.

aiReview.summary: Official API guide for JSON Search and Fetch endpoints that return ranked web results or Markdown page content for agents and RAG. Useful as a Resource, not a CLI or SDK package.
evidence: Page title Search & Fetch | DeepSeek API Docs; base URL https://api.deepseek.com.
Search supports query operators (site:, lang:, after:, etc.) and optional need_content; Fetch returns title and Markdown.
Billing and rate-limit sections present; auth is Bearer API key.
uncertainty: Live rate-limit numbers beyond the truncated page were not fully captured.
Account free-tier credits outside documented Search/Fetch pricing were not verified.
aiReview.tagline: JSON APIs to search the web and fetch Markdown pages
aiReview.description: POST Search and Fetch endpoints return ranked web results or Markdown content for agents and RAG, using bearer auth.
pros: Documents POST /v1/tools/search and /v1/tools/fetch with request fields, query operators, and response schemas.
Includes curl and Python examples plus OpenAI-compatible error status codes.
States per-request pricing ($0.75 per 1,000 successful calls) and when requests are not billed.
cons: It is vendor API documentation, not a standalone CLI, SDK, or open-source tool.
Listing title in the candidate was the generic link text “Click here to view the guide.”

aiReview.summary: Official docs for running OpenAI Codex Security scans in GitHub Actions (scheduled repo scans and PR diffs), with pinned Action/CLI versions, secrets setup, and severity policy. Useful as a CI companion to the CLI, not a standalone tool listing.
evidence: Canonical URL is OpenAI/ChatGPT developers docs: Run Codex Security in GitHub Actions.
Uses openai/codex-security@action-v0.3.0 and CODEX_SECURITY_API_KEY.
Discovered from curated OpenAI Codex docs as GitHub Actions.
uncertainty: Live Action maintenance and model availability (gpt-6-sol) were not independently verified.
Fit depends on whether the directory lists vendor CI docs vs. the CLI itself.
aiReview.tagline: CI workflows to scan repos and PRs with a security CLI
aiReview.description: Add GitHub Actions that install a security CLI, scan PRs or scheduled branches, and publish summaries, artifacts, and optional SARIF.
pros: Official documentation with pinned Action commit and CLI 0.3.0.
Covers scheduled repository scans and pull-request diff scans.
Documents secrets, sandbox setup, fail-on-severity, artifacts, and optional SARIF upload.
cons: Requires an OpenAI API key; scans incur usage charges.
Page title is generic GitHub Actions, not the product name.
Workflows skip fork PRs and Dependabot by default, so required checks can pass without a scan.
