aiReview.summary: This is a gaming-news article about unconfirmed GTA 6 leak clips and scams, not a command-line app or developer tool. It does not belong in an awesome-style CLI/utilities directory.
evidence: canonicalUrl and title are a gtaboom.com article about GTA 6 nude leak clips.
Rubric asks to score command-line apps and terminal utilities; this candidate is type web_url news.
discoveredFrom github_search but target is a blog post, not a maintained CLI repo.
uncertainty: Could not verify article body quality or scam-warning accuracy without fetching the page.
Publisher reputation and maintenance are unknown.
aiReview.tagline: Gaming news on unconfirmed GTA 6 leak clips
aiReview.description: Article arguing GTA 6 nude leak clips are unconfirmed and tied to scams. Not a CLI, SDK, or developer resource.
pros: Has a clear title and public URL.
Source appears to be a feed item rather than malware.
cons: Topic is celebrity/game leak gossip, not CLI or developer tooling.
Title and URL emphasize nude leaks, which is a poor fit and higher-risk content.
No GitHub-backed CLI, docs, or production utility is present.

aiReview.summary: Vendor docs for adding Firecrawl’s hosted MCP (search, scrape, parse) to Google Gemini CLI via settings.json. Useful as an integration listing, not a standalone CLI.
evidence: docs.firecrawl.dev/quickstarts/gemini-cli describes mcp.firecrawl.dev/v2/mcp and tools firecrawl_search, firecrawl_scrape, firecrawl_parse.
Discovered from Piebald-AI/awesome-gemini-cli README as Firecrawl.
uncertainty: Cannot verify current Firecrawl pricing tiers or GitHub maintenance from this page alone.
Cannot confirm Antigravity CLI replacement claims independently.
aiReview.tagline: Hosted MCP search and scrape for Gemini CLI
aiReview.description: Add hosted MCP search, scrape, and parse tools to Gemini CLI with a settings.json snippet and optional API key.
pros: Official docs show a concrete Gemini CLI MCP config and verification steps.
Documents keyless limits versus OAuth or API-key access.
Includes troubleshooting for missing tools after config changes.
cons: Page is product documentation, not a GitHub-backed CLI.
Keyless mode is IP-shared and exposes only three tools.
Notes Gemini CLI was replaced by Antigravity CLI for some users, which may age the listing.

aiReview.summary: Official Firecrawl docs for a remote MCP endpoint that agents can use without a key (rate-limited Search/Scrape/Parse) or with a bearer API key for more tools. Useful as an integration resource, not a standalone CLI.
evidence: Page states keyless URL https://mcp.firecrawl.dev/v2/mcp with no credential.
Keyless MCP is rate limited; API key unlocks full tool surface.
Discovered from Piebald-AI/awesome-gemini-cli README, not a GitHub CLI repo.
uncertainty: Current keyless quotas and commercial plan pricing were not verified on this page.
Runtime reliability of mcp.firecrawl.dev was not tested.
aiReview.tagline: Keyless remote MCP for web search, scrape, and parse
aiReview.description: Connect agents to a Streamable HTTP MCP URL with optional API key for higher limits and the full tool set.
pros: Official docs give copy-paste MCP configs for Codex, Claude Code, Cursor, OpenCode, and Droid.
Documents keyless vs API-key behavior, including which tools appear without credentials.
Links to local open-source server, tools list, and rate limits.
Source is vendor documentation, not a blog roundup.
cons: Candidate title is only “API key”; it is a docs page, not a CLI product.
Keyless mode is rate-limited and exposes only Search, Scrape, and Parse.
Hosted service requires trusting Firecrawl with scrape/search traffic; full surface needs a paid/plan API key.

aiReview.summary: Agent-oriented static hosting API: one PUT/POST publishes files to a permanent HTTPS subdomain with no signup. Useful for CLI/agent workflows; anonymous publish plus irrecoverable tokens if no recovery email is set.
evidence: Docs at https://deed.page/docs describe PUT/POST to /v1/sites and permanent https://{slug}.deed.page/ URLs.
Listed from Piebald-AI/awesome-gemini-cli as deed.page.
Skill repo cited as https://github.com/f-o-x11/deed-page-skill.
uncertainty: Long-term uptime, abuse handling, and paid-plan details beyond the free-plan snippet were not fully verified.
GitHub skill repo quality and maintenance were not inspected.
aiReview.tagline: One-request permanent static hosting for agents
aiReview.description: Publish files to a permanent HTTPS URL with one PUT or POST. No account required; token returned once for later updates.
pros: Docs specify a curl PUT/POST API, OpenAPI, MCP, and skill endpoints.
First publish needs no account; later updates use a Bearer token.
Free plan limits are documented: 25 sites, 25 MB per site, 60 publishes per hour.
Uploaded JS is not served on the deed.page origin; sites use slug subdomains.
cons: Tokens shown once cannot be recovered without optional email recovery.
Anonymous permanent hosting can be abused for unmoderated public content.
Free sites have no password protection.

aiReview.summary: Hosted personal CRM with remote MCP and OAuth so agents can read/write contacts, notes, tasks, and memory under user-approved scopes. Useful for agent workflows, but it is a SaaS MCP service rather than a CLI and is still in a free beta with an unproven long-term model.
evidence: Page title and copy: personal CRM designed for AI agents; MCP at https://withppl.com/mcp.
Setup snippets for Claude Code (`claude mcp add --transport http`) and Cursor mcp.json.
Claims 120 MCP tools and machine-readable spec at /.well-known/ppl.json.
Discovered as a one-word link from Piebald-AI/awesome-gemini-cli README.
uncertainty: Cannot verify GitHub presence, open-source status, or actual tool count without calling MCP.
Cannot verify security of token handling, data retention, or production reliability.
Post-beta pricing is unknown.
aiReview.tagline: Personal CRM MCP so agents recall people and tasks
aiReview.description: Hosted CRM and MCP server for contacts, notes, tasks, and memory. Agents connect with OAuth or tokens; humans approve scopes and can revoke access.
pros: Documents a hosted MCP URL, OAuth client setup for Claude, Claude Code, ChatGPT, and Cursor, plus a bearer-token path.
Describes scoped tokens, permission review, action logging, and revoke, plus REST and webhook APIs.
Free during beta with a stated 1,000-contact cap and no credit card.
Lists grouped tools for contacts, notes, tasks, reminders, journal, memory search, and briefings.
cons: Not a command-line app; it is a remote SaaS MCP/CRM, so it is a weak fit for a CLI-focused list.
Beta pricing and maintenance after launch are unspecified.
Contact and calendar imports depend on extra permissions and supported sources, not MCP alone.

aiReview.summary: Hosted MCP server that gives AI agents dedicated Cooper inboxes to create addresses, send/receive mail, search, and keep a human owner in the loop. Fits agent tooling lists; it is not a local CLI.
evidence: Docs at cooperemail.com/docs/mcp describe MCP at https://cooperemail.com/mcp.
Use cases include dedicated username@cooperemail.com inboxes, batch/TTL inboxes, and human-in-the-loop owners.
Free/Starter/Pro caps appear (e.g. batch count, custom domains, HTTP 402 plan_limit_exceeded).
Discovered from Piebald-AI/awesome-gemini-cli curated README.
uncertainty: Live uptime, spam reputation, and actual plan prices were not independently verified.
GitHub plugin repo quality and maintenance cadence were not reviewed in this pass.
aiReview.tagline: Hosted MCP inboxes for agents to send and receive mail
aiReview.description: Connect agents to a hosted MCP endpoint to create inboxes, send and search mail, and involve a human owner by email.
pros: Documents a Streamable HTTP MCP URL with OAuth 2.1+PKCE or Bearer API keys.
Lists many tools for inboxes, send/receive, search, drafts, webhooks, and owner tasks.
Notes it does not access a person’s existing mailbox; only Cooper inboxes.
Appears in the official MCP registry and several MCP directories.
Describes screening, suppressions, approval mode, and send-pause on bounce/complaint rates.
cons: cooper_onboard can create an account and live API key without prior auth.
Paid plans and Stripe add-ons apply; Free has inbox and domain limits.
Email bodies are untrusted; screening is heuristic, not a guarantee.

aiReview.summary: HTTP MCP endpoint that lets AI clients search a commercial software directory (listings, alternatives, trending) with no API key. Useful as an agent connector, not a standalone CLI utility.
evidence: Page title and copy: MCP Server at https://codetrendy.com/api/mcp, auth none, read-only, protocol 2025-06-18.
Claims 695 listings and tools such as search_listings, get_listing, find_alternatives, get_trending.
Founders section and pricing link show Verified listings ranked first with fuller agent-facing profiles.
Discovered from Piebald-AI/awesome-gemini-cli README with UTM referral parameters.
uncertainty: Cannot verify listing quality, MCP reliability, or GitHub maintenance from this page.
Cannot confirm whether the server is open-source or only a hosted endpoint.
Verified-plan pricing details were not fetched.
aiReview.tagline: Read-only MCP to search a public software directory
aiReview.description: Connect Claude, Cursor, ChatGPT, or VS Code to search listings, profiles, categories, and trending picks with one URL and no API key.
pros: Documents a public Streamable HTTP MCP URL with no authentication.
Lists seven read-only tools (search, listing, alternatives, categories, trending, site of the day).
Provides a one-line Claude Code install command and client setup notes.
cons: The product is a commercial directory MCP, not a GitHub-backed CLI or system utility.
Search ranking and payload richness favor paid Verified listings over free ones.
Site uses analytics cookies and optional session recording; MCP quality and listing count cannot be independently audited from the page alone.

aiReview.summary: Remote MCP endpoint for a commercial software directory: search listings, profiles, categories, and trending data with no API key. Useful as an agent tool, but it is not a maintained GitHub CLI and mixes directory SEO with paid listing promotion.
evidence: Page title and meta describe MCP for MediaProNet at https://mediapronet.com/api/mcp with auth none and read-only access.
Tools listed: search_listings, get_listing, find_alternatives, browse_category, list_categories, get_trending, get_site_of_the_day.
Discovered as a single-anchor listing in Piebald-AI/awesome-gemini-cli README with referral UTM.
Pricing CTA for Verified listings that rank first in agent search.
uncertainty: Cannot verify MCP server reliability, listing quality, or Gemini CLI compatibility beyond the marketing page.
Cannot verify GitHub presence, maintenance, or terms of use for bulk agent access.
aiReview.tagline: Read-only MCP access to a public software directory
aiReview.description: Point Claude, Cursor, ChatGPT, or VS Code at one HTTP MCP URL to search listings, read profiles, and fetch trending directory data.
pros: Documents a public Streamable HTTP MCP URL with no auth and seven read-only tools.
Provides a one-line Claude Code install command and example tool calls.
Server card and protocol version are linked from the page.
Scope is limited to public listing data and cannot mutate the site.
cons: Not a GitHub-backed CLI; it is a hosted directory MCP with UTM tracking from an awesome list.
Verified paid listings are ranked first and expose fuller profiles than free listings.
No open-source server implementation or changelog is shown on the page.
Session recording and analytics cookies are part of the site privacy posture.

aiReview.summary: Reference page that maps how to add the same MCP server (Context7) across Claude Code, Codex CLI, OpenCode, goose, and Gemini CLI, with copy-paste commands, config snippets, a cheat sheet, and dated official-doc sources.
evidence: Page title and H1: MCP servers, harness by harness; meta description matches CLI MCP setup comparison.
Sections for Claude Code, Codex CLI, OpenCode 1/2, goose, Gemini CLI plus Aider negative finding.
Sources list links to Claude, Codex, OpenCode, goose, and Gemini CLI MCP docs.
Discovered from Piebald-AI/awesome-gemini-cli curated README.
uncertainty: Cannot verify ongoing maintenance or accuracy of snippets after Oct 18, 2026.
Cannot verify operator identity beyond the contact email on the page.
No GitHub repo or license for the page content itself.
aiReview.tagline: Same MCP server, exact config for each coding CLI
aiReview.description: Compare MCP add commands and config files for Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, goose, and Gemini CLI, with scopes and gotchas.
pros: Shows equivalent MCP setup for multiple coding CLIs using one example server.
Includes CLI commands, config-file shapes, a harness cheat sheet, and FAQ notes on sharing configs.
Lists seven official documentation sources with a check date of Oct 18, 2026.
States there are no affiliate links and notes Aider has no documented MCP setup.
cons: Hosted on a Vercel marketing site with an email signup, not a GitHub-backed CLI repo.
Uses a single MCP server (Context7) as the worked example rather than a full catalog.
Config details can drift as harnesses change after the stated check date.

aiReview.summary: MIT-licensed macOS screenshot and screen-recording app (menu bar, Apple Silicon, macOS 14+) with annotation, scrolling capture, OCR, and video/GIF. Strong product page and GitHub, but it is a GUI Mac app, not a CLI, and install via curl|bash plus a personal domain warrant a human check.
evidence: Page states MIT, no account, Apple Silicon, macOS 14+, and GitHub at ciro-maciel/screenshots.
Features listed: 8 capture modes, 13 annotation tools, MP4/GIF recording, scrolling capture, Vision OCR, 30-day local history.
Compares itself to CleanShot X and built-in macOS capture; download is Screenshots-macos.dmg plus install.sh.
Discovered as Screenshots in jaywcjlove/awesome-mac.
uncertainty: Could not independently verify GitHub activity, release cadence, or that the binary truly has zero network code.
Could not verify notarization, malware scan, or install.sh contents.
English localization quality beyond the one-minute YouTube video is unclear.
aiReview.tagline: Local Mac capture, annotate, scroll, OCR, and record
aiReview.description: Capture, annotate, scroll-stitch, OCR, and record video or GIF on Mac with no cloud or account.
pros: Open source under MIT with a public GitHub repository.
Claims no network use, no account, and on-device OCR via Apple Vision.
Documents capture modes, editor tools, shortcuts, Screen Recording permission, and Apple notarization.
Free to download as a signed DMG for Apple Silicon and macOS 14+.
cons: GUI menu-bar app, not a command-line utility the CLI-focused rubric prefers.
Requires Apple Silicon; Intel Macs are unsupported.
Default install path is curl piped to bash from the author's blob host.
Product site is Portuguese-first and still lists gaps such as no dark mode or video trim.

aiReview.summary: Free, open-source macOS clipboard manager with history, saved snippets, and a paste queue; unsigned cask install and local encryption with a co-located key are the main caveats.
evidence: Project page: https://lorder19.github.io/clippo describes clipboard history, snippets, paste queue, and privacy behavior.
Listed from jaywcjlove/awesome-mac as Clippo.
Install paths: GitHub releases and brew install --cask lorder19/tap/clippo.
uncertainty: Did not inspect the GitHub repo for license, stars, or recent commit activity.
Did not verify binary signing, Accessibility use, or encryption implementation.
Paid extras mentioned as possible future work; current pricing beyond free is unknown.
aiReview.tagline: Keyboard-first clipboard history and paste queue for Mac
aiReview.description: Keep copy history, saved lists, and a paste queue on macOS 14+, skip concealed passwords, encrypt on disk, no account.
pros: Documents keyboard workflows: history (⌘;), numbered paste, saved lists, and a paste queue.
States it skips concealed password-manager copies and encrypts history on disk, with no account or analytics by default.
Distributed via GitHub releases and Homebrew cask; source is linked on GitHub.
Explicit privacy caveats: encryption key sits next to data, and some recorders ignore the private-window flag.
cons: Not a CLI; it is a macOS GUI/menu-bar app requiring Accessibility to synthesize paste.
Unsigned binary: install requires Open Anyway for an unidentified developer.
macOS 14+ only; author may add a paid tier later for extras such as rich-text formatting.

aiReview.summary: macOS 14+ menu-bar clipboard history app (⇧⌘V search/paste) that is MIT-licensed and local-only. Unsigned/not notarized, requires a quarantine workaround and Accessibility, and the author states it was generated with Claude Code with limited human review.
evidence: Site meta and body: free open-source clipboard history, ⇧⌘V, no network, macOS 14+, MIT.
Download points at GitHub turhe123/clip-recall-bar releases zip.
FAQ admits AI generation via Claude Code and unpaid Developer ID so no notarization.
Install instructs xattr -cr and Accessibility for paste injection.
uncertainty: GitHub stars, release recency, and code quality were not inspected beyond the marketing site.
Cannot verify absence of network code or malware without reviewing the binary/source.
Optional Ko-fi donate does not confirm ongoing maintenance.
aiReview.tagline: Keyboard-first local clipboard history in the macOS menu bar
aiReview.description: Keep copy history in the menu bar: filter as you type, paste with Return. Local files only; skips concealed/transient clips.
pros: MIT-licensed macOS 14+ universal binary with GitHub releases and source.
Documents keyboard paste/search, pin, ignore-apps, and skip of concealed/transient clipboard items.
States no network, accounts, or telemetry; history stored under Application Support as JSON/PNG.
Landing page covers install, Accessibility scope, and unsigned first-launch steps.
cons: Not notarized; first run needs right-click Open and xattr -cr on the app.
Author says the app was AI-generated with less human review than typical hand-written software.
Needs Accessibility to inject ⌘V; clipboard history is inherently sensitive data.

aiReview.summary: HTTP MCP endpoint that lets AI clients search a commercial software directory (listings, categories, trending). Paid Verified plans change search ranking and how much profile data agents receive.
evidence: Page title and meta describe MCP for Claude, Cursor, ChatGPT, and VS Code at https://sitepatent.com/api/mcp.
Tools listed: search_listings, get_listing, find_alternatives, browse_category, list_categories, get_trending, get_site_of_the_day.
Pricing CTA: Verified listings rank first and expose full description/tech stack to agents; free listings get a 160-character summary.
Discovered as a single-word link in Piebald-AI/awesome-gemini-cli README, not as a maintained CLI repo.
uncertainty: Cannot verify MCP server reliability, listing data accuracy, or GitHub source.
Cannot confirm whether the MCP is suitable for Gemini CLI beyond the awesome-list mention.
Pricing tiers beyond Verified vs free are not fully captured from this page.
aiReview.tagline: Read-only MCP access to a software listing directory
aiReview.description: Connect Claude, Cursor, ChatGPT, or VS Code to a public SaaS directory via one unauthenticated MCP URL.
pros: Documents seven read-only MCP tools and a streamable HTTP URL with no API key.
Provides a one-line Claude Code install command and client setup copy.
States protocol version 2025-06-18 and links a server-card JSON.
MCP access is unauthenticated and described as unable to mutate the site.
cons: It is a commercial directory MCP, not a GitHub-backed CLI or terminal utility.
Verified paid listings are returned first and with fuller agent-facing profiles than free listings.
The candidate URL includes referral UTM parameters from an awesome list.
Listing count is modest (page states 297 listings) and quality of directory entries is not independently verified.

aiReview.summary: Hosted remote MCP endpoint for preparing one 2025 US Form 1040 via an AI assistant, with review/sign/pay on a Terminal Tax page. Repo is docs and client manifests only; filing is a $19.99 paid service, not a local CLI.
evidence: GitHub README: Streamable HTTP MCP at https://mcp.terminal.tax/v1/hosted-mcp; tools create_filing_session, get_packet_schema, continue_filing_session.
Price stated as $19.99 per federal return charged only if IRS accepts.
About this repository: holds description, server.json, plugin manifests, logo, demos; no runnable server code.
Listed from Piebald-AI/awesome-gemini-cli-extensions as Terminal Tax.
uncertainty: Cannot independently verify IRS provider status, e-file reliability, or production security of mcp.terminal.tax.
Maintenance and 2026+ tax-year support are unknown beyond the 2025 scope in the README.
aiReview.tagline: Hosted MCP to prepare a 2025 Form 1040 for e-file
aiReview.description: Call a remote MCP server from an agent to assemble a 2025 federal 1040; the taxpayer reviews, signs, and pays on a hosted page.
pros: README documents JSON-RPC tools, endpoint URLs, scope limits, and that nothing is filed until the taxpayer signs.
States Terminal Tax LLC is an IRS Authorized e-file Provider and publishes privacy, terms, and support contacts.
Includes Gemini CLI, Cursor, and MCP client manifests plus a demo recording and transcript.
Repo is MIT-licensed documentation and config; the service is hosted, not local code to run.
cons: Repository has one star, no application source, and the live server is a third-party paid product.
Federal 1040/1040-SR only for tax year 2025; no state, amended, or extension returns.
Tax data and payment still flow through an AI-assisted hosted filing flow, which needs independent due-diligence.

aiReview.summary: Native macOS clipboard-history utility (SwiftUI/AppKit) with search, pin, paste-into-front-app, optional iCloud sync, and local-only storage. Fits awesome-mac-style CLI/desktop tooling lists as a maintained GitHub-backed Mac app, not a blog post.
evidence: Landing page at clipstack.chiranjeeb.dev describes clipboard history, ⇧⌘V panel, brew cask, GitHub releases.
Listed from jaywcjlove/awesome-mac README as Clipstack.
Privacy section states local history and optional private iCloud; MIT and GitHub star/sponsor links present.
uncertainty: Cannot verify GitHub activity, issue volume, or security of Accessibility usage from the marketing page alone.
Cannot confirm App Store approval status beyond “in review”.
aiReview.tagline: Native Mac clipboard history, one shortcut away
aiReview.description: Keeps Mac clipboard history locally. Search, pin, preview, and paste into the current app with a shortcut. Open source, no account.
pros: GitHub-backed MIT-licensed Mac app with Homebrew cask and signed/notarized DMG.
Features include search/filter, pin, rich previews, paste-as-plain-text, and optional iCloud sync off by default.
Privacy claims: local storage, skip concealed/transient copies, ignore-app list, no accounts or third-party SDKs.
Requires macOS 14+ and documents Accessibility use for pasting.
cons: Mac App Store listing is still in review.
macOS 14+ only, so older Macs are unsupported.
Needs Accessibility permission to paste into other apps.
